Script.name: mapper
Script.script:
--[[ Mapper — the MUSHclient mapper's commands, on Mudlet's map Sean Stoves, 2026-08-02
Same words, same order, same arguments. Someone moving across shouldn't have to relearn a workflow they already have in their fingers, and "it's the same thing but everything is called something else" is most of why people don't move.
The commands come from the MUSHclient mapper's own help - six sections, sixty-odd commands - and are reimplemented against Mudlet's map API. No code is taken from it: that plugin is Fiendish's and this is ours, written from the interface it publishes to its users.
What changes underneath, and why it can't not:
* There is one map per Mudlet profile, held by the client, not a SQLite file you point at. So 'mapper database' reports the profile's map and 'mapper set database' has nothing to set. 'mapper backup' still works - saveMap() writes a copy wherever you like.
* Notes are room user data, which lives inside the map file. MUSHclient kept them in a column. Same idea, and Mudlet can search them, which is how 'mapper notes' works without a full-text index.
* Custom exits are Mudlet special exits, which the client's own mapper already draws and already speedwalks through. That's the big win of moving: 'mapper cexit open south;;south' stops being a private thing the plugin knows and becomes an exit the whole client understands.
* Doors are real here. Mudlet has setDoor(room, dir, open|closed|locked) and draws each differently; MUSHclient had no such notion, which is why every door in your database is a cexit reading "open south;south". Those convert on import, and 'mapper door' marks them by hand.
Not built yet, and said out loud rather than quietly missing: the fifteen portal commands. They're their own bookkeeping - a portal list with indexes, bounce portals, level locks - and none of it maps onto anything Mudlet already has, so it's a module's worth of work on its own rather than a translation. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.mapper = aardkit.mapper or {}
local M = aardkit.mapper local U = aardkit.util.named("Mapper")
local CFG = U.load("mapper", { shownotes = true, quicklist = false, compact = false, updown = true, -- { { cmd, to, area, item, recall, level }, ... } -- -- 'to' is the room and 'area' is what the item's id box claims - "Leads to: -- The Amusement Park". They're different facts with different sources: the -- area comes off the item and is known before you ever use it, the room is -- only knowable by standing in it. Keeping both means a portal you haven't -- used yet is still listed, with what it's for, rather than absent until it -- has a room id. -- Ordered, because the whole interface addresses them by index: 'delete -- portal #3', 'bounceportal 2'. A map keyed on the command would read -- better and break every command anyone has written down. portals = {}, bounce = {}, -- { portal = <index>, recall = <index> } -- The portal wish gives you a wear location of its own, so a portal goes on -- without displacing anything and there's nothing to put back. Without it a -- portal is held, which costs you whatever was in that hand. Off by default -- because the held path works for everyone and the worn one doesn't. portalwish = false, -- ON. Installing this module takes the map over: if the stock AardwolfMudlet -- module is present its onRoom, its 'where' capture and its cp/quest map -- triggers are stood down, because two things writing one map is how rooms -- end up in the wrong place. If it isn't present there's nothing to stand -- down and this changes nothing. -- -- It is a switch, not a one-way door. 'mapper standalone off' hands the map -- straight back to theirs and 'mapper standalone' lists exactly what moved -- across in each direction. Nothing of theirs is deleted - only disabled. standalone = true, -- The master switch for walk.lua, separate from the one above so there's a -- way to stop writing without handing the map back to a module that may not -- be installed. mapwrite = true, -- Record a move that wasn't a direction as a custom exit, automatically. -- Off, and off on purpose: 'flee', 'recall' and 'enter' all change rooms, -- and a map that learns those ends up with a special exit out of every room -- you ever panicked in. 'mapper cexit <command>' is the deliberate version. autocexit = false, -- how the map draws; see style.lua. 'aard' is the MUSHclient mapper's own -- look - its background, its exit colour, square rooms, and its colours for -- shops, healers and banks - applied on load. That plugin's appearance is -- most of why people miss it, so matching it is the default rather than a -- command you have to know about. 'mapper style restore' puts your own -- Mudlet settings back; they're written down before anything is changed. style = "aard", stylewas = {}, -- your settings, saved before a style was applied -- On, because it's half of what the 'aard' style above IS - the loud fills -- for shops, healers and banks, plus a character so the colour says which. -- New rooms are marked as they're created; the ones already in the map need -- 'mapper style symbols' for this area or 'symbols all' for the lot. symbols = true, -- On. The continent drawn as boxes joined by strings is the thing that -- looks worst next to the MUSHclient map, and GMCP flags continent rooms so -- there's no guessing involved. Per area, so an inn keeps its corridors. autogrid = true, -- Draw the rooms GMCP has named but you've never entered, one step away -- with a '?' in them. On, because "there are four ways out of here I never -- took" is the single most useful thing a map can tell you. unexplored = true, -- Ours, not the stock module's. vconfig is part of a setup we don't own and -- may not be installed at all, so it's read as a convenience and never -- relied on: whatever is set here wins, and with neither set the chain is -- just hold-and-enter, which works if the portal is already in your hand. portalbag = "", portalback = "", -- what to put back after, e.g. "dual 3855651834" }) CFG.portals = CFG.portals or {} CFG.bounce = CFG.bounce or {}
local function save() U.save("mapper", CFG) end
-- walk.lua is the other half of this module and wants the same config and the -- same direction handling. Split across two files because the engine is a -- different job from the command tree, not because they're different modules. M.CFG = CFG M.save = save
local LONG = { n = "north", s = "south", e = "east", w = "west", u = "up", d = "down", ne = "northeast", nw = "northwest", se = "southeast", sw = "southwest", } local SHORT = {} for s, l in pairs(LONG) do SHORT[l] = s end
local function short_dir(cmd) cmd = U.trim(tostring(cmd or "")):lower() if LONG[cmd] then return cmd end if SHORT[cmd] then return SHORT[cmd] end return nil end
M.LONG = LONG M.short_dir = short_dir
local function here() local id = getPlayerRoom and getPlayerRoom() if not id or id == -1 then id = U.room() end return id end
local function areaname(id) local a = getRoomArea and getRoomArea(id) if not a then return "?" end -- getAreaTableSwap is id -> name, which is this question exactly. Every -- other call site here wants name -> id, which is getAreaTable - and for a -- while all of them called Swap and read it backwards. local ok, t = pcall(getAreaTableSwap) if ok and type(t) == "table" and t[a] then return t[a] end return tostring(a) end
M.areaname = areaname
--- -- the map panel -- -- The stock module builds its own Geyser.Mapper, wraps it in a plain -- Geyser.Container and nails it into GUIframe's topright frame. A plain -- container has no drag handles and saves no geometry, which is exactly why it -- sits where it sits and won't move. -- -- Ours is the same widget in an Adjustable.Container - drag it, resize it, dock -- or embed it, and it comes back where you left it, like every other panel -- here. Nothing clever: the difference is entirely which container it's in. -- -- Theirs is removed from the frame if it's there, because two mappers is worse -- than either. Only if it's there: no stock module, nothing to disable, and -- this is simply the map. ---
-- Same shape as the panel below it, and as every other widget in this suite: a -- local to work with, mirrored onto the module table for anything outside. It -- is NOT a bare global - theirs is one called 'mapwin', and copying a -- third-party module's namespacing for the sake of symmetry is not a reason. -- -- Unlike the panels this one gets reassigned, so the mirror sits on the line -- after each assignment where it can't drift out of sight of it. -- -- The Geyser widget underneath is still NAMED 'aardkitmap_<gen>_<seq>' - that's -- the Mudlet-level name, and that one does want a distinctive prefix. -- -- It started life as a local called 'mapwin', the same name as theirs, and the -- line meant to put THEIR map view back was quietly moving ours. What fixed -- that was the rename, not where the reference is kept. local map -- Bumped every time ours is rebuilt. Mudlet keeps a Geyser widget alive under -- its name, so remaking one with the same name leaves the old object orphaned -- on top of the new one - and this gets remade whenever the stock module's map -- turns up after ours. Declared here, above everything that reads it. local seq = 0
local panel = aardkit.panel.new({ -- 'map' was taken. The ASCII Map module registers a panel under that name -- too, and a second registration REPLACES the first and hides its holder - -- so whichever loaded second owned the name, the geometry and the title, -- and the other one was a hidden frame nobody could find. This module lost, -- which is why the map panel came up empty with 'ASCII Map' on it. name = "mapper", title = "Mapper", x = "10px", y = "40px", width = 420, height = 420, consoleless = true, -- No background. The map is drawn at absolute coordinates in the main -- window rather than inside this container, so a background here is painted -- over the map, not behind it - which is the map "fading" until something -- repaints it. It was a tinted sheet of glass the whole time. clear = true, onbuild = function() map = nil M.map = nil if aardkit.mapper and aardkit.mapper.paint_map then aardkit.mapper.paint_map() end end, onresize = function() if aardkit.mapper and aardkit.mapper.paint_map then aardkit.mapper.paint_map() end end, })
M.panel = panel
-- Returns false and a reason rather than just giving up quietly. A blank panel -- with no explanation is the worst of both - it looks like the map is broken -- when the answer is usually that the container isn't up yet. function M.paint_map() if not panel.container then return false, "the panel hasn't been built yet" end if not map then -- gen-suffixed like every other widget here: Mudlet keeps the old object -- alive across a dock switch and reusing the name orphans it local ok, w = pcall(function() return Geyser.Mapper:new({ -- gen and seq suffixed: Mudlet keeps a Geyser object alive -- under its name, so reusing one after a dock switch rebuilds -- the container orphans the old widget on top of the new one name = "aardkitmap_" .. (panel.gen or 1) .. "_" .. tostring(seq), x = 0, y = 0, width = "100%", height = "100%", }, panel.container) end) if not ok then return false, tostring(w) end if not w then return false, "Geyser.Mapper gave nothing back" end map = w M.map = map end pcall(function() map:resize("100%", "100%") end) pcall(function() map:move(0, 0) end) pcall(function() map:show() end) M.raise_map() return true end
-- An embedded Mudlet map is not a child of the container it looks like it's in. -- createMapper draws it at absolute coordinates in the main window, so every -- other Geyser element is a candidate to land on top of it - which is what the -- greyed-out map that comes back when you click it actually is. -- -- raiseWindow("mapper") is what Geyser.Mapper:raise() does; this is the same -- call somewhere it can be reached from. function M.raise_map() if not U.has("raiseWindow") then return false end return (pcall(raiseWindow, "mapper")) end
-- Take the map view back. -- -- There is only ONE. Mudlet's own Geyser.Mapper says so in as many words - -- "mappers are typically singleton per profile" - and every method underneath -- proves it: raise() is raiseWindow("mapper"), and an embedded mapper is just -- createMapper(window, x, y, w, h) pointed somewhere. Two Geyser.Mapper objects -- aren't two maps, they're two claims on the same one, and the last claim wins. -- -- The stock module builds its map on a timer AFTER this script has run, so at -- load ours is made first and theirs second, theirs wins, and our panel comes up -- empty with nothing to say about why. This is that fix: reposition() re-runs -- createMapper with our geometry, which claims it back. -- -- Deliberately NOT a fresh Geyser.Mapper each time. Every orphan left behind is -- another object Geyser may call reposition() on later, and any one of them -- doing so would steal the view to wherever it used to be. function M.repaint_map() if not panel.container then return false, "the panel hasn't been built yet" end if not map then return M.paint_map() end -- reposition() bails on a hidden widget, so show first pcall(function() map:show() end) pcall(function() map:resize("100%", "100%") end) pcall(function() map:move(0, 0) end) local ok, err = pcall(function() map:reposition() end) if not ok then return false, tostring(err) end M.raise_map() return true end
-- Take the stock module's map out of its frame, if that module is installed at -- all. Their widget stays alive and hidden rather than deleted - it isn't ours -- to destroy, and a reinstall of theirs just gets removed again next load. -- Their map is a Geyser.Mapper called 'mapwin' inside a Geyser.Container called -- 'mapcontainer' - ours is the widget named 'aardkitmap' - put into the frame with -- addWindow(mapcontainer, "Map", -- "topright"). removeWindow throws if GUIframe hasn't initialised yet, which on -- a slow load it hasn't - and this used to return true regardless, so it -- announced it had taken their map out while the map was still sitting there. -- -- Now it reports what actually happened, and the widgets get hidden by name -- whatever removeWindow managed, because hiding is the part that matters. function M.unframe_theirs() if not GUIframe then return false end if not (GUIframe.removeWindow and GUIframe.initialized) then return false end
local ok = pcall(GUIframe.removeWindow, "Map", "topright") if not ok then ok = pcall(GUIframe.removeWindow, "Map") end
-- The graphical map only. Their 'minimap' is the MUD's own ASCII map, which -- is a different thing built from different data and nothing here replaces -- it - unless our own ASCII Map module is installed, in which case two of -- them is one too many. local targets = { "mapcontainer", "mapwin" } if U.have("asciimap") then targets[#targets + 1] = "minimap" end
local hid = false for _, name in ipairs(targets) do local w = _G[name] if type(w) == "table" and w.hide then if pcall(function() w:hide() end) then hid = true end end end return ok or hid end
-- The other direction. Whatever this module takes it has to be able to give -- back, or 'standalone' is a one-way door with a switch drawn on it. function M.reframe_theirs() if not GUIframe then return false end local shown = false for _, name in ipairs({ "mapcontainer", "mapwin", "minimap" }) do local w = _G[name] if type(w) == "table" and w.show then if pcall(function() w:show() end) then shown = true end end end if GUIframe.addWindow and GUIframe.initialized and type(mapcontainer) == "table" then pcall(GUIframe.addWindow, mapcontainer, "Map", "topright") end -- and the map view itself, which is a singleton: theirs has to claim it -- back or it stays wherever ours last put it local theirmap = _G.mapwin if type(theirmap) == "table" and theirmap.reposition then pcall(function() theirmap:reposition() end) end return shown end
--- -- notes -- -- Room user data, so they're saved inside the map rather than in a file beside -- it, and searchRoomUserData can find them - which is what 'mapper notes' and -- 'mapper find' are built on. ---
local NOTE = "note"
local function get_note(id) if not (id and getRoomUserData) then return nil end local ok, v = pcall(getRoomUserData, id, NOTE) if ok and v and v ~= "" then return v end return nil end
function M.addnote(text) local id = here() if not id then U.warn("Mudlet doesn't know which room you're in."); return end text = U.trim(text) if text == "" then local cur = get_note(id) U.note(cur and ("Note on " .. U.rid(id) .. ": " .. cur) or "No note here. 'mapper addnote <text>' to add one.") return end pcall(setRoomUserData, id, NOTE, text) U.ok("Noted on " .. U.rid(id) .. ": " .. text) end
function M.delnote() local id = here() if not id then return end if not get_note(id) then U.note("No note here."); return end pcall(clearRoomUserData, id, NOTE) U.ok("Note removed from " .. U.rid(id) .. ".") end
--- -- searching ---
-- rows -> a numbered, clickable result list you can 'mapper next' through local last_results = {}
local function results(title, list) last_results = list if #list == 0 then U.note("Nothing found."); return end U.note(#list .. " result(s) - click one, or 'mapper next' to walk them:") for i, r in ipairs(list) do if i > 30 then U.out("\n <#8a93a8>... " .. (#list - 30) .. " more<r>"); break end U.out(string.format("\n <#8a93a8>%2d<r> <#c8d0dc>%s<r> <#8a93a8>%s<r>", i, r.name or "?", r.area or "")) if r.note then U.out("\n <#e0af68>" .. r.note .. "<r>") end U.outLink(" <#3ad07a>[go]<r>", "aardkit.mapper.goto_room(" .. r.id .. ")", "Speedwalk to " .. U.rid(r.id), true) end echo("\n") end
local function scope_rooms(scope) scope = U.trim(tostring(scope or "")):lower() if scope == "" then return nil end -- everywhere local id = here() if scope == "here" then local a = id and getRoomArea and getRoomArea(id) return a and select(2, pcall(getAreaRooms, a)) or nil end local ok, t = pcall(getAreaTable) if ok and type(t) == "table" then for name, aid in pairs(t) do if name:lower():find(scope, 1, true) then return select(2, pcall(getAreaRooms, aid)) end end end return nil end
local function in_scope(id, allowed) if not allowed then return true end for _, rid in ipairs(allowed) do if rid == id then return true end end return false end
function M.find(text, scope) text = U.trim(text) if text == "" then U.warn("Usage: mapper find <text>"); return end local allowed = scope_rooms(scope) local out, seen = {}, {} local ok, rooms = pcall(searchRoom, text) if ok and type(rooms) == "table" then for rid, name in pairs(rooms) do local id = tonumber(rid) or rid if not seen[id] and in_scope(id, allowed) then seen[id] = true out[#out + 1] = { id = id, name = name, area = areaname(id), note = get_note(id) } end end end -- and anything whose note mentions it, which is the half MUSHclient's -- full-text search had and a plain room-name search doesn't local ok2, hits = pcall(searchRoomUserData, NOTE, text) if ok2 and type(hits) == "table" then for _, rid in pairs(hits) do local id = tonumber(rid) if id and not seen[id] and in_scope(id, allowed) then seen[id] = true out[#out + 1] = { id = id, name = getRoomName and getRoomName(id) or "?", area = areaname(id), note = get_note(id) } end end end table.sort(out, function(a, b) return (a.area or "") < (b.area or "") end) results("find", out) end
-- rooms carrying a given Aardwolf flag, which the importer stored as 'info' local function flagged(want, scope) local allowed = scope_rooms(scope) local out = {} local ok, hits = pcall(searchRoomUserData, "info", want) if ok and type(hits) == "table" then for _, rid in pairs(hits) do local id = tonumber(rid) if id and in_scope(id, allowed) then out[#out + 1] = { id = id, name = getRoomName and getRoomName(id) or "?", area = areaname(id), note = get_note(id) } end end end return out end
function M.notes(scope) local allowed = scope_rooms(scope) local out = {} local ok, hits = pcall(getAllRoomUserData and function() return nil end or function() return nil end) -- searchRoomUserData with an empty needle isn't defined, so walk the areas local areas = {} local okt, t = pcall(getAreaTable) if okt and type(t) == "table" then for _, aid in pairs(t) do areas[#areas + 1] = aid end end for _, aid in ipairs(areas) do local okr, rooms = pcall(getAreaRooms, aid) if okr and type(rooms) == "table" then for _, id in pairs(rooms) do local n = get_note(id) if n and in_scope(id, allowed) then out[#out + 1] = { id = id, name = getRoomName and getRoomName(id) or "?", area = areaname(id), note = n } end end end end results("notes", out) end
function M.goto_room(id) id = tonumber(id) if not id then return end if not (roomExists and roomExists(id)) then U.warn("Room " .. tostring(id) .. " isn't in the map."); return end local from = here() if not from then U.warn("Mudlet doesn't know where you are."); return end if not (getPath and getPath(from, id)) then U.warn("No known path to " .. U.rid(id) .. " from here.") return end -- Not doSpeedWalk(). The stock module replaces that global with its own - -- 'run = buildSpeedWalk(); display(run); send(run)' - so calling it hands -- our route to their implementation and prints the command at you. S&D has -- avoided it since it was written; this had not. local steps = {} for i, d in ipairs(speedWalkDir or {}) do steps[i] = d end if #steps == 0 then U.warn("No route to " .. U.rid(id) .. "."); return end U.ok("Walking to " .. U.rid(id) .. " - " .. #steps .. " step(s).") -- S&D already folds runs of basic directions into 'run 3n2e'. Use it if -- that module is here; send the steps one at a time if it isn't. local compress = aardkit.snd and aardkit.snd.compress local cmds = compress and compress(steps) or steps for _, c in ipairs(cmds) do send(c, false) end end
local next_i = 0
function M.next(idx) idx = tonumber(idx) if idx then next_i = idx - 1 end if #last_results == 0 then U.note("No search results to walk."); return end next_i = next_i + 1 if next_i > #last_results then next_i = 1 end local r = last_results[next_i] U.note("Result " .. next_i .. " of " .. #last_results .. ": " .. (r.name or "?")) M.goto_room(r.id) end
function M.where(id) id = tonumber(U.trim(id)) if not id then U.warn("Usage: mapper where <room id>"); return end local from = here() if not (from and getPath and getPath(from, id)) then U.warn("No known path to " .. tostring(id) .. ".") return end U.note(#speedWalkDir .. " step(s) to " .. U.rid(id) .. ":") U.out("\n <#c8d0dc>" .. table.concat(speedWalkDir, ", ") .. "<r>") U.outLink(" <#3ad07a>[walk it]<r>", "aardkit.mapper.goto_room(" .. id .. ")", "Speedwalk there", true) echo("\n") end
--- -- exploring ---
function M.thisroom() local id = here() if not id then U.warn("Mudlet doesn't know which room you're in."); return end local rows = { { "id", U.rid(id) }, { "name", getRoomName and getRoomName(id) or "?" }, { "area", areaname(id) }, } -- 'a and f()' keeps one return value, not three, so y and z came back nil local x, y, z if U.has("getRoomCoordinates") then x, y, z = getRoomCoordinates(id) end if x then rows[#rows + 1] = { "coords", string.format("%d, %d, %d", x, y or 0, z or 0) } end local okd, info = pcall(getRoomUserData, id, "info") if okd and info and info ~= "" then rows[#rows + 1] = { "flags", info } end local n = get_note(id) if n then rows[#rows + 1] = { "note", n } end
local ex = (getRoomExits and getRoomExits(id)) or {} local dirs = {} for d in pairs(ex) do dirs[#dirs + 1] = d end table.sort(dirs) if #dirs > 0 then rows[#rows + 1] = { "exits", table.concat(dirs, " ") } end
local doors = (getDoors and select(2, pcall(getDoors, id))) or {} if type(doors) == "table" then local ds = {} for d, st in pairs(doors) do ds[#ds + 1] = d .. "=" .. ({ [1] = "open", [2] = "closed", [3] = "locked" })[st] end table.sort(ds) if #ds > 0 then rows[#rows + 1] = { "doors", table.concat(ds, " ") } end end
local sp = (getSpecialExits and select(2, pcall(getSpecialExits, id))) or {} if type(sp) == "table" then for dest, cmd in pairs(sp) do rows[#rows + 1] = { "cexit", tostring(cmd) .. " -> " .. U.rid(dest) } end end U.help("Room", rows) end
function M.areas(filter) filter = U.trim(tostring(filter or "")):lower() local ok, t = pcall(getAreaTable) if not ok or type(t) ~= "table" then U.warn("No areas in the map."); return end local names = {} for name in pairs(t) do if filter == "" or name:lower():find(filter, 1, true) then names[#names + 1] = name end end table.sort(names) if #names == 0 then U.note("No areas matching '" .. filter .. "'."); return end local rows = {} for _, name in ipairs(names) do local okr, rooms = pcall(getAreaRooms, t[name]) local n = (okr and type(rooms) == "table") and #rooms or 0 rows[#rows + 1] = { name, n .. " rooms" } end U.help(#names .. " area(s)", rows) end
function M.showroom(id) id = tonumber(U.trim(id)) if not id then U.warn("Usage: mapper showroom <room id>"); return end if not (roomExists and roomExists(id)) then U.warn("Room " .. id .. " isn't in the map."); return end pcall(centerview, id) U.ok("Map centred on " .. U.rid(id) .. ".") end
-- an exit that goes nowhere yet: Mudlet calls these stubs function M.unmapped(scope) local allowed = scope_rooms(scope == "" and "here" or scope) if not allowed then U.warn("Usage: mapper unmapped [here|<area>]"); return end local rows, total = {}, 0 for _, id in ipairs(allowed) do -- A '?' room is an unmapped exit that got drawn instead of stubbed, so -- it belongs in this list or the count reads as zero the moment the -- engine starts drawing them. local oku, u = pcall(getRoomUserData, id, "unexplored") if oku and u == "1" then total = total + 1 if #rows < 30 then rows[#rows + 1] = { U.rid(id), "never entered - '?' on the map" } end else local ok, stubs = pcall(getExitStubs, id) if ok and type(stubs) == "table" and #stubs > 0 then total = total + #stubs if #rows < 30 then rows[#rows + 1] = { U.rid(id) .. " " .. (getRoomName and getRoomName(id) or "?"), #stubs .. " unmapped" } end end end end if total == 0 then U.ok("No unmapped exits there."); return end U.help(total .. " unmapped exit(s)", rows) end
--- -- custom exits ---
function M.cexits(scope) local allowed = scope_rooms(scope == "" and "here" or scope) if not allowed then U.warn("Usage: mapper cexits [here|<area>]"); return end local rows = {} for _, id in ipairs(allowed) do local ok, sp = pcall(getSpecialExits, id) if ok and type(sp) == "table" then for dest, cmd in pairs(sp) do rows[#rows + 1] = { tostring(cmd), U.rid(id) .. " -> " .. U.rid(dest) } end end end if #rows == 0 then U.note("No custom exits there."); return end table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a[1] < b[1] end) U.help(#rows .. " custom exit(s)", rows) end
-- 'mapper cexit <command>' - run it, see where you end up, link it. MUSHclient -- used ;; to get a multi-command cexit past its line parser; keep that so the -- syntax people have written down still works. local pending
function M.cexit(cmd) cmd = U.trim(cmd) if cmd == "" then U.warn("Usage: mapper cexit <command> (';;' separates steps)"); return end local from = here() if not from then U.warn("Mudlet doesn't know where you are."); return end pending = { from = from, cmd = cmd } U.note("Following '" .. cmd .. "' from " .. U.rid(from) .. " - it'll link when you arrive.") for raw in (cmd .. ";;"):gmatch("(.-);;") do local step = U.trim(raw) local wait = step:match("^wait%((%d+)%)$") if wait then -- their syntax for a pause mid-cexit elseif step ~= "" then send(step, false) end end end
-- "Magic walls bounce you back." is what a room that refuses portals and recalls -- actually says. It's instant and certain, which beats waiting six seconds to -- conclude nothing happened, and it means a room gets marked the first time you -- try rather than after the timeout. function M.on_blocked() local id = here() if not id then return end pcall(setRoomUserData, id, "noportal", "1") if adding then local item = adding.item adding = nil U.warn("Magic walls: '" .. item .. "' won't fire here. Room marked noportal.") else U.note("Magic walls here - room marked noportal.") end end
-- and its recall counterpart, which is a different flag function M.on_norecall() local id = here() if not id then return end pcall(setRoomUserData, id, "norecall", "1") U.note("Can't recall from here - room marked norecall.") end
-- room.info arriving after a cexit or a 'portal add' is what tells us where it -- went. Both wait on the same event; neither can be pending at once because -- each is started by a command you typed. function M.on_room() if adding then local to = here() local a = adding if to and to ~= a.from then adding = nil M.portal_record(a.cmd, to, a.item) return end end if not pending then return end local to = here() local p = pending pending = nil if not to or to == p.from then return end pcall(addSpecialExit, p.from, to, p.cmd) U.ok("Linked: " .. U.rid(p.from) .. " -> " .. U.rid(to) .. " '" .. p.cmd .. "'") -- 'open south;;south' is a door and Mudlet can say so, which MUSHclient never could local d = short_dir((p.cmd:gsub("^%s*open%s+", ""):gsub(";.*$", ""))) if d and p.cmd:lower():match("^%s*open%s") then pcall(setDoor, p.from, d, 2) U.note("...and marked a closed door " .. (LONG[d] or d) .. ".") end end
function M.fullcexit(cmd, from, to) from, to = tonumber(from), tonumber(to) if not (cmd and from and to) then U.warn("Usage: mapper fullcexit {<command>} <source> <destination>") return end if not (roomExists(from) and roomExists(to)) then U.warn("One of those rooms isn't in the map."); return end pcall(addSpecialExit, from, to, cmd) U.ok("Linked: " .. U.rid(from) .. " -> " .. U.rid(to) .. " '" .. cmd .. "'") end
function M.delcexits() local id = here() if not id then return end local ok, sp = pcall(getSpecialExits, id) local n = 0 if ok and type(sp) == "table" then for dest, cmd in pairs(sp) do pcall(removeSpecialExit, id, cmd) n = n + 1 end end U.ok("Removed " .. n .. " custom exit(s) from " .. U.rid(id) .. ".") end
function M.delexits(which, room) room = tonumber(U.trim(room)) local id = here() if not (room and id) then U.warn("Usage: mapper delete exits from|to <room id>"); return end local a, b = room, id if which == "to" then a, b = id, room end local ok, sp = pcall(getSpecialExits, a) local n = 0 if ok and type(sp) == "table" then for dest, cmd in pairs(sp) do if dest == b then pcall(removeSpecialExit, a, cmd); n = n + 1 end end end U.ok("Removed " .. n .. " exit(s) " .. which .. " " .. U.rid(room) .. ".") end
--- -- doors — beyond MUSHclient, because Mudlet can draw them ---
function M.door(rest) local id = here() if not id then return end local dir, what = U.split_verb(rest) local d = short_dir(dir) if not d then -- no direction: show what this room has local doors = (getDoors and select(2, pcall(getDoors, id))) or {} local rows = {} if type(doors) == "table" then for dd, st in pairs(doors) do rows[#rows + 1] = { LONG[dd] or dd, ({ [1] = "open", [2] = "closed", [3] = "locked" })[st] or "?" } end end if #rows == 0 then U.note("No doors recorded here. 'mapper door <dir> closed|locked|open|none'.") else table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a[1] < b[1] end) U.help("Doors in " .. U.rid(id), rows) end return end what = U.trim(what):lower() local st = ({ none = 0, open = 1, closed = 2, locked = 3 })[what] if not st then U.warn("Usage: mapper door <dir> none|open|closed|locked"); return end pcall(setDoor, id, d, st) U.ok("Door " .. (LONG[d] or d) .. " marked " .. what .. ".") end
--- -- portals -- -- A hand-held portal is a command that puts you somewhere, and the somewhere is -- the room you're standing in when you record it - unlike a cexit, which is -- walked to find out. That's the MUSHclient behaviour and it's the right one: -- you buy a portal, use it, and record where it landed you. -- -- Recall Manager already does the firing half of this - a named entry holding -- commands - so this is the same idea with a destination attached and an index, -- because every portal command addresses them by number. -- -- noportal / norecall are room facts, not portal facts, so they live in room -- user data beside the notes rather than in this list. ---
local function portal_line(i, p) local dest if p.to then dest = (getRoomName and getRoomName(p.to) or "?") .. " " .. U.rid(p.to) else dest = (p.area or "?") .. " <#e0af68>room unknown - use it and 'mapper portal'<r>" end local bits = { p.cmd } if p.item then bits[#bits + 1] = "(" .. p.item .. ")" end if p.recall then bits[#bits + 1] = "(recall)" end if (p.level or 0) > 0 then bits[#bits + 1] = "(level " .. p.level .. ")" end if CFG.bounce.portal == i then bits[#bits + 1] = "<bounce portal>" end if CFG.bounce.recall == i then bits[#bits + 1] = "<bounce recall>" end return table.concat(bits, " "), dest end
function M.portals(scope) if #CFG.portals == 0 then U.note("No portals recorded. Stand where one drops you and 'mapper portal <command>'.") return end local allowed = scope_rooms(scope) local rows = {} for i, p in ipairs(CFG.portals) do if in_scope(p.to, allowed) then local a, b = portal_line(i, p) rows[#rows + 1] = { "#" .. i .. " " .. a, b } end end if #rows == 0 then U.note("No portals to there."); return end U.help(#rows .. " portal(s)", rows) end
-- What the id box said this portal leads to, if the Loot Tracker has seen one. -- Optional in both directions: no tracker, no item, or no 'Leads to' just means -- the area stays unknown and the room is still recorded. local function item_for(cmd) local LT = aardkit.loot if not (LT and LT.t and LT.t.item_stats) then return nil end local kw = tostring(cmd or ""):match("^%s*%a+%s+(%S+)") if not kw then return nil end local ok, rows = pcall(db.fetch, db, LT.t.item_stats, db:AND(db:eq(LT.t.item_stats.type, "Portal"), db:like(LT.t.item_stats.keywords, "%" .. kw .. "%"))) if not ok or type(rows) ~= "table" or not rows[1] then return nil end return rows[1] end
-- One place that knows how to run a portal, because two would drift: this is -- what 'portal add' fires to find the room, and what Search and Destroy fires -- when it routes through one. ';;' separates steps, same as a cexit. function M.fire_portal(p) local cmd = type(p) == "table" and p.cmd or tostring(p or "") for raw in (cmd .. ";;"):gmatch("(.-);;") do local step = U.trim(raw) if step ~= "" then send(step, false) end end end
-- Using a portal is five commands, not one: -- -- get <portal> <bag>;hold <portal>;enter;dual <weapon>;put <portal> <bag> -- -- Take it out, equip it, use it, put back whatever it displaced, stow it. The -- bag and the weapon come from the stock module's own vconfig - the same place -- Healme reads its potion from - so there's no second copy to go stale and no -- serial numbers written down here. -- -- Without that module it falls back to 'hold <item>;;enter', which works if the -- portal is already in your hands. Nothing requires anything. -- ours first, the stock module's only if it happens to be there local function cfgval(mine, theirs) local v = U.trim(tostring(CFG[mine] or "")) if v ~= "" then return v end local c = aard and aard.config v = c and theirs and c[theirs] v = U.trim(tostring(v or "")) return v ~= "" and v or nil end
local function portal_chain(item) local bag = cfgval("portalbag", "pbag") local steps = {} if bag and bag ~= "" then steps[#steps + 1] = "get " .. item .. " " .. bag end
if CFG.portalwish then -- its own wear location: nothing is displaced, so nothing goes back steps[#steps + 1] = "wear " .. item steps[#steps + 1] = "enter" else steps[#steps + 1] = "hold " .. item steps[#steps + 1] = "enter" -- put back whatever that hand was holding local back = U.trim(tostring(CFG.portalback or "")) if back == "" then local c = aard and aard.config local d = c and c["dual"] local w = c and c["wield"] if d and d ~= "" then back = "dual " .. d elseif w and w ~= "" then back = "wield " .. w end end if back ~= "" then steps[#steps + 1] = back end end
if bag and bag ~= "" then steps[#steps + 1] = "put " .. item .. " " .. bag end return table.concat(steps, ";;") end
M.portal_chain = portal_chain
-- 'mapper portal add <item>' - use it here and now, and record where you land. -- -- The alternative was "go and stand where it drops you, then type the command", -- which asks you to do the travelling and the bookkeeping both. The client -- knows the room the moment room.info arrives. local adding
function M.portal_add(item) item = U.trim(item) if item == "" then U.warn("Usage: mapper portal add <item> (a keyword for the portal you carry)") return end local from = here() if not from then U.warn("Mudlet doesn't know which room you're in."); return end
-- Rooms that refuse portals are a fact worth checking before spending five -- commands finding out. If you've marked this one, or the MUD told us once -- already, don't try. local ok, np = pcall(getRoomUserData, from, "noportal") if ok and np == "1" then U.warn("This room is marked noportal - a portal won't fire from here.") U.note("Move somewhere it works, or 'mapper noportal " .. from .. " false' if that's wrong.") return end
local cmd = portal_chain(item) adding = { cmd = cmd, item = item, from = from } local _, joins = cmd:gsub(";;", "") U.note("Using '" .. item .. "' - " .. (joins + 1) .. " step(s), and the room you land in gets recorded.") M.fire_portal(adding)
-- The backstop. "Magic walls bounce you back." arrives instantly when the -- room refuses, so this only fires when something else went wrong - you -- weren't carrying it, the keyword was off, the bag was shut. tempTimer(6, function() if adding and adding.from == from then adding = nil pcall(setRoomUserData, from, "noportal", "1") U.warn("Portal '" .. item .. "' didn't move you. Marked this room noportal" .. " so it won't be tried from here again.") U.note("If it failed for some other reason: 'mapper noportal " .. from .. " false'.") end end) end
-- you are standing where it put you function M.portal(cmd) cmd = U.trim(cmd) if cmd == "" then U.warn("Usage: mapper portal <command> (stand where it drops you)"); return end local id = here() if not id then U.warn("Mudlet doesn't know which room you're in."); return end return M.portal_record(cmd, id, nil) end
function M.portal_record(cmd, id, kw) local it = item_for(kw and ("enter " .. kw) or cmd) local area = it and U.trim(tostring(it.leads_to or "")) or "" local iname = it and it.item or nil local where = areaname(id)
for i, p in ipairs(CFG.portals) do if p.cmd:lower() == cmd:lower() then p.to = id if area ~= "" then p.area = area end if iname then p.item = iname end save() U.ok("Portal #" .. i .. " '" .. cmd .. "' now lands in " .. U.rid(id) .. " (" .. where .. ")") return end end CFG.portals[#CFG.portals + 1] = { cmd = cmd, to = id, area = area ~= "" and area or nil, item = iname, recall = false, level = 0, } save() U.ok("Portal #" .. #CFG.portals .. ": '" .. cmd .. "' -> " .. U.rid(id) .. " (" .. where .. ")") -- the item said an area; the map says a room. If they disagree it's worth -- seeing, because it usually means the portal was used from the wrong place. if area ~= "" and where ~= "?" and area:lower() ~= where:lower() then U.warn("The item says it leads to '" .. area .. "' but you're in '" .. where .. "'. Recorded the room you're in.") end end
local function portal_at(spec) spec = U.trim(tostring(spec or "")) local n = tonumber(spec:match("^#?(%d+)$")) if n then return n, CFG.portals[n] end for i, p in ipairs(CFG.portals) do if p.cmd:lower() == spec:lower() then return i, p end end return nil end
function M.portalrecall(spec) local i, p = portal_at(spec) if not p then U.warn("No portal '" .. tostring(spec) .. "'."); return end p.recall = not p.recall; save() U.ok("Portal #" .. i .. " '" .. p.cmd .. "' " .. (p.recall and "uses a recall." or "no longer flagged as a recall.")) end
function M.portallevel(spec, lvl) local i, p = portal_at(spec) if not p then U.warn("No portal '" .. tostring(spec) .. "'."); return end local n = math.floor(tonumber(lvl) or -1) if n < 0 then U.warn("Usage: mapper portallevel <index> <level>"); return end p.level = n; save() U.ok("Portal #" .. i .. " level lock: " .. (n == 0 and "none" or n) .. ".") end
-- 'bounceportal 2' says which portal to route through for a noportal room; -- bare shows it, 'clear' drops it function M.bounce(kind, arg) arg = U.trim(tostring(arg or "")) if arg == "" then local i = CFG.bounce[kind] local p = i and CFG.portals[i] U.note("Bounce " .. kind .. ": " .. (p and ("#" .. i .. " '" .. p.cmd .. "'") or "not set")) return end if arg:lower() == "clear" then CFG.bounce[kind] = nil; save() U.ok("Bounce " .. kind .. " cleared.") return end local i, p = portal_at(arg) if not p then U.warn("No portal '" .. arg .. "'."); return end CFG.bounce[kind] = i; save() U.ok("Bounce " .. kind .. ": #" .. i .. " '" .. p.cmd .. "'.") end
function M.delportal(spec) local i = portal_at(spec) if not i then U.warn("No portal '" .. tostring(spec) .. "'."); return end local p = table.remove(CFG.portals, i) -- the indexes below it just moved, so a bounce pointing past it has to follow for _, k in ipairs({ "portal", "recall" }) do local b = CFG.bounce[k] if b == i then CFG.bounce[k] = nil elseif b and b > i then CFG.bounce[k] = b - 1 end end save() U.ok("Removed portal '" .. p.cmd .. "'.") end
function M.changeportal(spec, newcmd) local i, p = portal_at(spec) if not p then U.warn("No portal '" .. tostring(spec) .. "'."); return end newcmd = U.trim(newcmd) if newcmd == "" then U.warn("Usage: mapper change portal {<old>} {<new>}"); return end local was = p.cmd p.cmd = newcmd; save() U.ok("Portal #" .. i .. ": '" .. was .. "' -> '" .. newcmd .. "'.") end
function M.purgeportals() local n = #CFG.portals CFG.portals, CFG.bounce = {}, {} save() U.ok("Removed " .. n .. " portal(s).") end
-- room facts, stored beside the notes function M.roomflag(which, rest) local id, val = U.split_verb(rest) id = tonumber(U.trim(id)) or here() if not id then U.warn("Usage: mapper " .. which .. " <room id> [true|false]"); return end val = U.trim(val):lower() if val == "" then local ok, v = pcall(getRoomUserData, id, which) U.note(U.rid(id) .. " " .. which .. ": " .. ((ok and v == "1") and "yes" or "no")) return end if val == "true" or val == "yes" or val == "1" then pcall(setRoomUserData, id, which, "1") U.ok(U.rid(id) .. " marked " .. which .. ".") else pcall(clearRoomUserData, id, which) U.ok(U.rid(id) .. " no longer " .. which .. ".") end end
-- Portal items you own, if the Loot Tracker happens to be installed. -- -- Nothing here requires it. Aardwolf's id box gives 'Type: Portal' and a -- 'Leads to:' naming the destination AREA, and the Loot Tracker already parses -- and keeps that - so if it's there, this can tell you which portals you own -- and which you haven't recorded yet. If it isn't, you add them by hand with -- 'mapper portal <command>' exactly as before and nothing is missing. -- -- An area name isn't a room, so this deliberately doesn't guess a destination. -- It lists what you have and leaves the recording to the one thing that knows -- for certain: you, standing where the portal dropped you. function M.portals_learn() local LT = aardkit.loot if not (LT and LT.t and LT.t.item_stats) then U.note("Nothing to read portal items from - record them by hand with" .. " 'mapper portal <command>' while standing where one drops you.") U.suggest("loot", "It reads 'Type: Portal' and 'Leads to:' off an id box, so you'd" .. " only confirm the room.") return end local ok, rows = pcall(db.fetch, db, LT.t.item_stats, db:eq(LT.t.item_stats.type, "Portal")) if not ok or type(rows) ~= "table" or #rows == 0 then U.note("No portal items in the loot database yet - 'id <portal>' while holding one.") return end local known = {} for _, p in ipairs(CFG.portals) do known[p.cmd:lower()] = true end
local added, rowsout = 0, {} for _, r in ipairs(rows) do local dest = U.trim(tostring(r.leads_to or "")) local kw = U.trim(tostring(r.keywords or "")):match("^(%S+)") or "" local cmd = kw ~= "" and ("enter " .. kw) or nil local have = cmd and known[cmd:lower()] if cmd and not have then -- an entry with the area filled and no room yet. It shows in the -- list as something you own and haven't located, which is the point: -- a portal you've never used is still worth knowing you have. CFG.portals[#CFG.portals + 1] = { cmd = cmd, to = nil, area = dest ~= "" and dest or nil, item = r.item, recall = false, level = 0, } added = added + 1 end rowsout[#rowsout + 1] = { r.item, (dest ~= "" and dest or "?") .. (have and " already recorded" or "") } end if added > 0 then save() end table.sort(rowsout, function(a, b) return a[1] < b[1] end) U.help(#rowsout .. " portal item(s) you've identified", rowsout) U.ok(added .. " added to the portal list.") U.note("The id box only names an area, which isn't a room. Use one and" .. " 'mapper portal <command>' where it drops you to fill in the room id.") end
-- Which recorded portal, if any, gets us within reach of `dest`. Returns the -- portal and how many steps remain after it lands. -- -- Only if one is present. This never invents a route: no portals recorded means -- nil, and whatever asked carries on as it did before. -- -- getPath writes speedWalkDir as a side effect, so the caller has to run its own -- getPath afterwards - the one left behind here is for whichever portal won. function M.portal_for(dest) dest = tonumber(dest) if not (dest and roomExists and roomExists(dest)) then return nil end if #CFG.portals == 0 then return nil end local best, bestn for _, p in ipairs(CFG.portals) do if p.to and roomExists(p.to) then if p.to == dest then return p, 0 end if getPath(p.to, dest) then local n = #(speedWalkDir or {}) if not bestn or n < bestn then best, bestn = p, n end end end end return best, bestn end
--- -- utils ---
function M.backup(path) path = U.trim(path) if path == "" then path = getMudletHomeDir() .. "/map-backup-" .. getTime(true, "yyyyMMdd-hhmm") .. ".dat" end local ok, err = pcall(saveMap, path) if ok then U.ok("Map saved to " .. path) else U.err("Couldn't save the map: " .. tostring(err)) end end
function M.purgeroom() local id = here() if not id then return end pcall(deleteRoom, id) U.ok("Room " .. U.rid(id) .. " deleted from the map.") end
function M.purgezone(name) name = U.trim(name) if name == "" then U.warn("Usage: mapper purgezone <area>"); return end local ok, t = pcall(getAreaTable) if not ok or type(t) ~= "table" then return end for area, aid in pairs(t) do if area:lower() == name:lower() then pcall(deleteArea, aid) U.ok("Deleted area '" .. area .. "'.") return end end U.warn("No area called '" .. name .. "'.") end
-- Theirs, and what replaces it on this side. Named so 'mapper standalone' can -- say what it's switching off rather than just doing it. local THEIRS = { { "onRoom", "script", "writes rooms and exits on every move", "this module, via their own aard.map.enable flag" }, { "where", "trigger", "'Players near you' capture", "Player Tracker, and 'mapper where <room>' for directions" }, { "map quest cp gq", "trigger", "campaign and quest target capture", "Search and Destroy's own capture and panel" }, }
--- -- the command tree ---
local function onoff(v, cur) v = U.trim(tostring(v or "")):lower() if v == "on" then return true elseif v == "off" then return false end return not cur end
function M.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) rest = U.trim(rest)
-- exploring if verb == "thisroom" then M.thisroom() elseif verb == "showroom" then M.showroom(rest) elseif verb == "areas" then M.areas(rest) elseif verb == "unmapped" then M.unmapped(rest)
-- searching elseif verb == "find" then M.find(rest) elseif verb == "area" then M.find(rest, "here") elseif verb == "list" then M.find(rest) elseif verb == "notes" then M.notes(rest) elseif verb == "shops" then results("shops", flagged("shop", rest)) elseif verb == "train" then results("trainers", flagged("trainer", rest)) elseif verb == "quest" then results("quest givers", flagged("quest", rest)) elseif verb == "next" then M.next(rest) elseif verb == "where" then M.where(rest)
-- exits elseif verb == "cexits" then M.cexits(rest) elseif verb == "cexit" then M.cexit(rest) elseif verb == "fullcexit" then local cmd, a, b = rest:match("^%s*{(.-)}%s*(%d+)%s+(%d+)") M.fullcexit(cmd, a, b) elseif verb == "lockexit" then U.note("Mudlet has no level locks; use 'mapper door' for doors, or room weights for pathing.")
-- doors (ours) elseif verb == "door" then M.door(rest)
-- the engine elseif verb == "mapping" then M.mapstat(rest) elseif verb == "style" then M.style(rest) elseif verb == "autocexit" then CFG.autocexit = onoff(rest, CFG.autocexit); save() U.ok("Non-direction moves recorded as custom exits: " .. (CFG.autocexit and "on" or "off")) if CFG.autocexit then U.note("'flee' and 'recall' change rooms too - expect some tidying with 'mapper delete cexits'.") end
-- utils elseif verb == "addnote" then M.addnote(rest) elseif verb == "backup" then M.backup(rest) elseif verb == "purgeroom" then M.purgeroom() elseif verb == "purgezone" then M.purgezone(rest)
elseif verb == "delete" then local what, more = U.split_verb(rest) more = U.trim(more) if what == "note" then M.delnote() elseif what == "cexits" then M.delcexits() elseif what == "portal" then M.delportal(more) elseif what == "exits" then local dirn, room = U.split_verb(more) if dirn == "from" or dirn == "to" then M.delexits(dirn, room) else U.warn("Usage: mapper delete exits from|to <room id>") end else U.warn("mapper delete note | cexits | portal <cmd|#n> | exits from|to <room>") end
elseif verb == "purge" then local what, more = U.split_verb(rest) if what == "portals" then M.purgeportals() elseif what == "cexits" then local scope = U.trim(more):lower() == "area" and "here" or nil local rooms = scope and scope_rooms("here") or nil local n = 0 local list = rooms if not list then list = {} local okt, t = pcall(getAreaTable) if okt then for _, aid in pairs(t) do local okr, rr = pcall(getAreaRooms, aid) if okr and type(rr) == "table" then for _, r in pairs(rr) do list[#list + 1] = r end end end end end for _, id in ipairs(list) do local ok, sp = pcall(getSpecialExits, id) if ok and type(sp) == "table" then for _, cmd in pairs(sp) do pcall(removeSpecialExit, id, cmd); n = n + 1 end end end U.ok("Removed " .. n .. " custom exit(s).") else U.warn("mapper purge cexits [area] | portals") end
-- config elseif verb == "zoom" then -- Bigger is closer. This had it the other way round, so 'mapper zoom in' -- zoomed out - settled by watching it: the stock module sets 35 and a -- saved override of 10 is what turned every room into a two-pixel dot. local d = U.trim(rest):lower() local n = tonumber(d) local z = (getMapZoom and getMapZoom()) or 20 if n then pcall(setMapZoom, math.max(1, math.floor(n))) U.ok("Zoom " .. math.max(1, math.floor(n)) .. ".") elseif d == "in" or d == "out" then local to = d == "in" and (z + 3) or math.max(1, z - 3) pcall(setMapZoom, to) U.ok("Zoom " .. d .. " - now " .. to .. ".") else U.help("mapper zoom", { { "now", tostring(z) }, { "" }, { "mapper zoom in | out", "three at a time" }, { "mapper zoom <n>", "straight to a number; bigger is closer" }, { "" }, { "The MUSHclient map draws a 12px room with 8px between it and" }, { "the next, so 20 is what its cells measure. That's the style's." }, }) end
elseif verb == "show" or verb == "hide" or verb == "dock" or verb == "embed" then aardkit.panel.cmd("mapper " .. verb) -- after the move, not before: dock and embed rebuild the container and -- a mapper parented to the old one goes with it if verb ~= "hide" then M.repaint_map() end
elseif verb == "standalone" then -- Hiding their map widget leaves their mapping running underneath: -- onRoom is hooked to gmcp.room and writes rooms, exits and coordinates -- on every move, same as ours would. Two things writing one map is how -- you get rooms in the wrong place. -- -- This is the switch, and it is not free. Their speedwalk, coordrun, -- 'where', and the cp/quest map triggers all read what onRoom wrote, so -- they stop working too. That's the trade: you've replaced them, or you -- haven't and shouldn't touch this. local v = U.trim(rest):lower() if v ~= "on" and v ~= "off" then local rows = { { "state", CFG.standalone and "on - ours has the map" or "off - theirs is running too" }, { "writing", M.mapping() and "ours is creating rooms" or (M.why_not_mapping() or "?") } } if type(aard) == "table" and type(aard.map) == "table" then rows[#rows + 1] = { "their mapper", aard.map.init and "running" or "stood down via aard.map.enable" } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } for _, t in ipairs(THEIRS) do rows[#rows + 1] = { t[1] .. " (" .. t[2] .. ")", t[3] } rows[#rows + 1] = { "", "-> " .. t[4] } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "mapper standalone on", "ours maps, theirs stands down" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "mapper standalone off", "theirs maps again, ours stops writing" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "mapper reframe", "just hand their map widget back" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Their mapping goes down through their own aard.map.enable, not by" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "disabling their script - so nothing of theirs is touched that they" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "didn't put a switch on. Swap back and forth as often as you like." } U.help("Standalone mapping", rows) return end if not U.has("disableScript") then U.warn("This Mudlet has no disableScript, so their mapping can't be switched off.") return end if not (aard and GUIframe) then U.note("The stock module isn't installed, so there's nothing to stand down - " .. "ours already has the map. 'mapper mapping' for what it's doing.") return end CFG.standalone = (v == "on") save() local theirs = their_map(v ~= "on") for _, t in ipairs(THEIRS) do if not (theirs and t[1] == "onRoom") then aardkit.stock.cmd((v == "on" and "off " or "on ") .. t[1]) end end stood_down = (v == "on") U.ok(v == "on" and "Stock mapping off - ours has the map to itself." or "Stock mapping back on. Reload to be sure it's running.") if v == "on" then M.unframe_theirs() M.repaint_map() U.note("Walk a few rooms and check 'mapper mapping'. Only new rooms are ever " .. "placed - nothing already in the map gets moved or renamed.") else -- Mudlet draws into the map view that was made last, so leaving ours -- up would keep it rather than theirs. Ours goes; theirs comes back -- with the reload, because we can't rebuild somebody else's widget. if map then pcall(function() map:hide() end) end panel:hide() unframed = false M.reframe_theirs() U.note("Ours is down and theirs is back in its frame. Reload if anything looks half-done.") end
elseif verb == "map" or verb == "panel" then -- Show first, paint second. Geyser will parent a mapper into a hidden -- container and then draw nothing into it, which looks exactly like a -- broken map and isn't. panel:show() local ok, why = M.repaint_map() panel:raise() if ok then U.ok("Map panel up. Drag it, resize it, 'mapper dock' or 'mapper embed' to move it.") else U.err("Couldn't put a map in the panel: " .. tostring(why)) if GUIframe then U.note("The stock module has a map view too. 'mapper unframe' takes it down, then try again.") end end
elseif verb == "reframe" then if not GUIframe then U.note("The stock module isn't installed - there's nothing to hand back to.") else their_map(true) M.reframe_theirs() unframed, stood_down = false, false U.ok("Their map is back: widget reframed and aard.map.enable set.") U.note("This is display and mapping only - 'mapper standalone off' is the full swap.") end
elseif verb == "unframe" then if not GUIframe then U.note("The stock module isn't installed - there's no embedded map to remove.") elseif M.unframe_theirs() then M.repaint_map() U.ok("Stock map hidden, and ours rebuilt so it's the one being drawn into.") else U.warn("Couldn't reach it - GUIframe " .. (GUIframe.initialized and "is up but wouldn't remove it." or "hasn't initialised yet; try again in a moment.")) end elseif verb == "shownotes" then CFG.shownotes = onoff(rest, CFG.shownotes); U.save("mapper", CFG) U.ok("Notes in search results: " .. (CFG.shownotes and "on" or "off")) elseif verb == "quicklist" then CFG.quicklist = onoff(rest, CFG.quicklist); U.save("mapper", CFG) U.ok("Quicklist: " .. (CFG.quicklist and "on" or "off")) elseif verb == "compact" then CFG.compact = onoff(rest, CFG.compact); U.save("mapper", CFG) U.ok("Compact output: " .. (CFG.compact and "on" or "off")) elseif verb == "updown" then CFG.updown = onoff(rest, CFG.updown); U.save("mapper", CFG) U.ok("Up/down drawing: " .. (CFG.updown and "on" or "off")) elseif verb == "database" then U.note("Mudlet keeps one map per profile: " .. getMudletHomeDir() .. "/map" .. " 'mapper backup <path>' writes a copy.")
elseif verb == "portals" then if U.trim(rest):lower() == "learn" then M.portals_learn() else M.portals(rest) end elseif verb == "portal" then local sub, more = U.split_verb(rest) if sub == "add" then M.portal_add(more) else M.portal(rest) end elseif verb == "portalbag" then CFG.portalbag = U.trim(rest); save() U.ok(CFG.portalbag ~= "" and ("Portals live in '" .. CFG.portalbag .. "'.") or "Portal bag cleared - portals are assumed to be in hand already.") U.note("Chain: " .. portal_chain("<item>"):gsub(";;", " ;; "))
elseif verb == "portalback" or verb == "portalrestore" then CFG.portalback = U.trim(rest); save() U.ok(CFG.portalback ~= "" and ("After entering: '" .. CFG.portalback .. "'.") or "Nothing put back after entering.") U.note("Chain: " .. portal_chain("<item>"):gsub(";;", " ;; "))
elseif verb == "portalwish" then CFG.portalwish = onoff(rest, CFG.portalwish); save() U.ok("Portal wish: " .. (CFG.portalwish and "on - portals are worn, nothing is displaced." or "off - portals are held, and whatever was in that hand goes back after.")) U.note("Chain: " .. portal_chain("<item>"):gsub(";;", " ;; "))
elseif verb == "portalrecall" then M.portalrecall(rest) elseif verb == "portallevel" then local a, b = U.trim(rest):match("^(%S+)%s+(%S+)") M.portallevel(a, b) elseif verb == "bounceportal" then M.bounce("portal", rest) elseif verb == "bouncerecall" then M.bounce("recall", rest) elseif verb == "noportal" or verb == "norecall" then M.roomflag(verb, rest)
elseif verb == "change" then local what, more = U.split_verb(rest) if what ~= "portal" then U.warn("mapper change portal {<old>} {<new>}"); return end local old, new = more:match("^%s*{(.-)}%s*{(.-)}") if not old then old, new = more:match("^%s*(#%d+)%s*{(.-)}") end if not old then U.warn("mapper change portal {<old>} {<new>} or #<index> {<new>}"); return end M.changeportal(old, new)
else M.help(verb) end end
function M.help(which) if which == "exits" then U.help("mapper - exits", { { "mapper cexits [here|<area>]", "list custom exits" }, { "mapper cexit <command>", "run it and link where you end up (';;' between steps)" }, { "mapper fullcexit {<cmd>} <from> <to>", "link without walking it" }, { "mapper delete cexits", "remove this room's custom exits" }, { "mapper delete exits from|to <room>", "remove exits between here and there" }, { "mapper purge cexits [area]", "remove them everywhere, or in this area" }, { "mapper door <dir> none|open|closed|locked", "mark a door (Mudlet draws each differently)" }, }) elseif which == "portals" then U.help("mapper - portals", { { "mapper portals [here|<area>]", "list them" }, { "mapper portals learn", "portal items you own, if Loot Tracker is installed" }, { "mapper portal add <item>", "hold it, enter it, and record where you land" }, { "mapper portal <command>", "record it by hand - stand where it drops you" }, { "mapper portalwish on|off", "you have the portal wish, so portals are worn not held" }, { "mapper portalbag <bag>", "where you keep them; empty means already in hand" }, { "mapper portalback <cmd>", "what to re-equip after, e.g. 'dual 12345'" }, { "mapper portalrecall <#>", "flag it as using a recall" }, { "mapper portallevel <#> <n>", "level lock, 0 for none" }, { "mapper bounceportal [#|clear]", "which portal to route through for a noportal room" }, { "mapper bouncerecall [#|clear]", "the same for norecall" }, { "mapper noportal|norecall [<room>] [true|false]", "mark a room" }, { "mapper change portal {<old>} {<new>}", "rename the command" }, { "mapper delete portal <cmd|#n>", "remove one" }, { "mapper purge portals", "remove them all" }, }) elseif which == "search" or which == "searching" then U.help("mapper - searching", { { "mapper find <text>", "search room names and notes, everywhere" }, { "mapper area <text>", "the same, this area only" }, { "mapper notes [here|<area>]", "rooms you've noted" }, { "mapper shops|train|quest [here|<area>]", "rooms flagged as such" }, { "mapper where <room id>", "directions from here" }, { "mapper next [n]", "walk to the next result" }, }) else U.help("mapper", { { "mapper thisroom", "everything known about where you're standing" }, { "mapper areas [name]", "areas and their room counts" }, { "mapper showroom <id>", "centre the map somewhere else" }, { "mapper unmapped [here|<area>]", "exits that lead nowhere yet" }, { "" }, { "mapper find <text>", "search names and notes ('mapper help search' for more)" }, { "mapper addnote <text>", "note this room" }, { "mapper delete note", "remove it" }, { "" }, { "mapper cexit <command>", "custom exits ('mapper help exits' for more)" }, { "mapper door <dir> closed|locked", "mark a door" }, { "" }, { "mapper mapping", "what the engine is doing, and whether it's on" }, { "mapper style aard", "draw it like the MUSHclient map - tiles and terrain colours" }, { "mapper backup [path]", "write a copy of the map" }, { "mapper purgeroom | purgezone <area>", "delete a room or an area" }, { "mapper map", "the map panel - drag it, resize it, it stays put" }, { "mapper unframe", "hide the stock module's embedded map, by hand" }, { "mapper reframe", "give it straight back to them" }, { "mapper standalone on|off", "stop the stock module writing to the map too" }, { "mapper show|hide|dock|embed", "where the map panel lives" }, { "mapper zoom in|out", "map zoom" }, { "" }, { "mapper portals", "hand-held portals ('mapper help portals' for more)" }, { "" }, { "Same commands as the MUSHclient mapper, on Mudlet's own map." }, }) end end
aardkit.register("mapper", "the MUSHclient mapper's commands, on Mudlet's map", M.cmd)
-- One watcher, not two. walk.lua's engine has to create the room before -- on_room() can link a cexit or a portal to it, and two watchers on the same -- path fire in pairs() order, which is to say in whichever order they feel like -- that session. So the engine is the entry point and calls on_room() when it's -- finished. aardkit.gmcp.watch("mapper_room", "room.info", "aardkit.mapper.on_move", true)
-- The stock module builds its map on sysLoadEvent behind a 0.1s timer, so this -- has to land after that or there's nothing in the frame to remove yet. It -- retries because their timing is theirs, not ours. local unframed, stood_down = false, false
-- Their own switch, which is better than ours. -- -- Their config script has `aard.map.enable`, guiLoad does -- `if (aard.map.enable) then aard:init_map() end`, init_map sets -- `aard.map.init = true`, and onRoom's second line is -- `if not (aard.map.init) then return end`. So the flag is the supported way to -- stop their mapper, and it beats disabling the script by name on every count: -- it's what their author put there for this, it survives them renaming a script -- out from under us, and it can't half-fail the way a name lookup can. -- -- It's also more precise. The guard sits BELOW the line that keeps -- aard.map.current_room up to date, so their other pieces that read that go on -- working - only the writing stops, which is the only part we're replacing. -- -- `enable` is for their next load, `init` is for right now. Both, so it takes -- effect immediately and stays taken. local function their_map(on) if type(aard) ~= "table" or type(aard.map) ~= "table" then return false end aard.map.enable = on and true or false if on then -- init_map builds the state tables parseGmcpRoom then reads. Setting -- init true without them would have their mapper raise on the next room -- rather than map it. if type(aard.init_map) == "function" then pcall(aard.init_map, aard) else aard.map.init = false end else aard.map.init = false end return true end
M.their_map = their_map
local function stand_down() if stood_down or not CFG.standalone then return end if not aard then return end
-- their switch first; ours only for the pieces it doesn't cover local theirs = their_map(false) if not (theirs or U.has("disableScript")) then return end
for _, t in ipairs(THEIRS) do -- onRoom is handled by the flag above, and disabling the script as well -- would stop the current_room bookkeeping their other pieces still want if not (theirs and t[1] == "onRoom") then aardkit.stock.cmd("off " .. t[1]) end end stood_down = true U.note("Stock mapping stood down - two things writing one map is how rooms end up" .. " in the wrong place. 'mapper standalone' lists what moved across, and" .. " 'mapper standalone off' hands it straight back.") end
local function claim_map() -- Before the unframed check, not after. Taking their map out of the frame -- can succeed on the first pass while 'aard' isn't loaded yet, and with this -- below the early return the retries never came back round to it - their -- mapping stayed on with ours running too, which is the one state to avoid. stand_down() if not CFG.standalone then return end local got = M.unframe_theirs() if got and not unframed then unframed = true -- Theirs is built after ours and the last map view made is the one -- Mudlet draws into, so ours comes back blank until it's remade now -- that theirs is down. This is the whole reason the panel was empty. M.repaint_map() U.note("Took the stock module's map out of its fixed frame - 'mapper map' for ours.") end end
M.paint_map()
-- Five passes rather than three, and they keep hiding on every pass rather than -- stopping at the first success. Their GUIframe loads its saved layout after we -- run and puts the map back in the frame, so a single removal early on gets -- undone and nobody is told. 'mapper unframe' does it by hand at any point. for _, t in ipairs({ 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 }) do tempTimer(t, claim_map) end

Script.name: mapper/walk
Script.script:
--[[ Mapper — the mapping engine Sean Stoves, 2026-08-02
What actually creates rooms as you walk. Until this file existed the module was a reader: it searched, noted, linked cexits, drew a panel — but the rooms themselves came from the stock module's onRoom, which is the whole reason 'mapper standalone' had to stay off.
Built from Aardwolf's GMCP and Mudlet's map API. The arithmetic — two units per step on x and y, one on z, y inverted on the continent — is what the map format needs, not anyone's code.
One rule shapes everything below: an existing room is never moved, never renamed, never re-areaed. There are 23,000 rooms in an imported map with coordinates that took a layout pass to compute, and a mapper that second-guesses them is a mapper that ruins them. New rooms get placed. Old rooms only ever get blanks filled in.
So the worst this can do is put a NEW room somewhere daft, and 'mapper purgeroom' undoes that. ]]
local M = aardkit.mapper local U = aardkit.util.named("Mapper") local CFG = M.CFG
--- -- direction tables -- -- Mudlet's exit numbering. Not alphabetical, not compass order — this is the -- order its map format uses, and the reverse table below is the check: walk the -- pairs and every one comes back to itself. ---
local DIRNUM = { n = 1, ne = 2, nw = 3, e = 4, w = 5, s = 6, se = 7, sw = 8, u = 9, d = 10 } local REVNUM = { 6, 8, 7, 5, 4, 1, 3, 2, 10, 9 }
-- two per step on the flat, one per floor. Two so a room can be nudged aside -- without landing on its neighbour, which is the only reason it isn't one. local STEP = { n = { 0, 2, 0 }, s = { 0, -2, 0 }, e = { 2, 0, 0 }, w = { -2, 0, 0 }, ne = { 2, 2, 0 }, nw = { -2, 2, 0 }, se = { 2, -2, 0 }, sw = { -2, -2, 0 }, u = { 0, 0, 1 }, d = { 0, 0, -1 }, }
-- The same directions at one unit. Kept as its own table rather than dividing -- STEP by two, because in Lua 5.3 and later '/' hands back a float and Mudlet -- wants whole coordinates - and the float propagates into every room reckoned -- from that one afterwards. local UNIT = { n = { 0, 1, 0 }, s = { 0, -1, 0 }, e = { 1, 0, 0 }, w = { -1, 0, 0 }, ne = { 1, 1, 0 }, nw = { -1, 1, 0 }, se = { 1, -1, 0 }, sw = { -1, -1, 0 }, u = { 0, 0, 1 }, d = { 0, 0, -1 }, }
-- where to try when the spot is taken. Flat only: shoving a room up a floor to -- avoid an overlap is more confusing than the overlap. local NUDGE = { { 2, 0 }, { -2, 0 }, { 0, 2 }, { 0, -2 }, { 2, 2 }, { -2, 2 }, { 2, -2 }, { -2, -2 }, }
--- -- terrain -> environment -- -- The ids are the ones the MUSHclient map used, so a room this engine creates -- comes out the same colour as the 23,000 that came across in the import rather -- than a second palette sitting next to the first. -- -- Colours are registered on first use, not all at load: 134 setCustomEnvColor -- calls for the six terrains you'll actually walk through tonight is work for -- nothing. ---
local PALETTE = { [0] = { 0, 0, 0 }, [1] = { 128, 0, 0 }, [2] = { 0, 128, 0 }, [3] = { 128, 128, 0 }, [4] = { 0, 0, 128 }, [5] = { 128, 0, 128 }, [6] = { 0, 128, 128 }, [7] = { 192, 192, 192 }, [8] = { 128, 128, 128 }, [9] = { 255, 0, 0 }, [10] = { 0, 255, 0 }, [11] = { 255, 255, 0 }, [12] = { 0, 0, 255 }, [13] = { 255, 0, 255 }, [14] = { 0, 255, 255 }, [15] = { 255, 255, 255 }, }
-- terrain name -> { env id, palette index } local TERRAIN = { inside={1,7}, city={2,7}, field={3,2}, forest={4,10}, hills={5,2}, mountain={6,3}, waterswim={7,12}, waternoswim={8,12}, unused={9,7}, air={10,14}, desert={11,11}, ocean={12,4}, quicksand={13,3}, underwater={14,4}, ice={15,15}, underground={16,4}, road_eastwest={17,7}, road={18,7}, river={19,4}, volcano={20,9}, cave={21,4}, dungeon={22,8}, road_crossroads={23,7}, mudschool={24,7}, areaexit={25,5}, hellinside={26,9}, hellfountain={27,9}, hell1={28,9}, hell2={29,9}, hell3={30,9}, insideice={31,15}, hellhall={32,9}, hell4={33,9}, smallroad={34,7}, smallroad_ew={35,7}, trail_ew={36,3}, beach={37,3}, shore={38,6}, jungle={39,2}, swamp={40,2}, bridge={41,7}, plain={42,3}, ocean2={43,12}, ocean3={44,12}, ocean4={45,12}, field3={46,2}, field2={47,2}, field4={48,2}, rocks={49,3}, snow={50,15}, icemount={51,15}, icehills={52,15}, space1={53,8}, space2={54,8}, space3={55,8}, space4={56,8}, castle={57,7}, pillar={58,7}, dark={59,8}, crossroad_nw={60,7}, crossroad_se={61,7}, crossroad_ews={62,7}, mountain_cyan={63,6}, moon={64,4}, temple={65,7}, shop={66,2}, clanexit={67,7}, chessblack={68,4}, chesswhite={69,15}, lottery={70,7}, alley={71,8}, fountain={72,6}, archive={73,7}, bookshelves={74,7}, bookshelves_ns={75,7}, office={76,5}, electric={77,7}, well={78,7}, bloodyhall={79,9}, bloodyroom={80,9}, dead_forest={81,3}, dead_field={82,3}, graveyard={83,8}, palace_room={84,7}, crypt={85,4}, dead_jungle={86,3}, ship={87,7}, chaos_sea={88,7}, hut={89,7}, redcarpet={90,9}, city_underground={91,8}, mist={92,8}, ashen_field={93,3}, cabin={94,7}, hallway={95,7}, afountain={97,7}, flowers1={98,7}, flowers2={99,7}, stairs={100,7}, aylorcity={101,7}, ruins={102,7}, tornado={103,8}, dustdevil={104,7}, wind1={105,7}, wind2={106,7}, lightning={107,7}, rain={108,8}, sun={109,11}, cloud1={110,7}, cloud2={111,8}, cloud3={112,7}, rainbow={113,14}, fiery_cave={114,7}, tunnel={115,7}, vertical_shaft={116,7}, interestpoint={117,7}, redtemple={118,7}, redgateway={119,7}, slashone={120,7}, slashtwo={121,7}, slashthree={122,7}, slashfour={123,7}, crater={124,7}, forest2={125,10}, xspot={126,9}, spacered={127,1}, redcircle={128,1}, bluecircle={129,7}, darkspace={130,8}, whitespace={131,7}, rose={132,9}, peony={133,13}, vine={134,11}, violet={135,5}, }
-- Set every time rather than once per session. There was a cache here and it -- bought nothing measurable - this runs when a room is CREATED, not on every -- move - while quietly going stale the moment anything wiped the map, which -- 'aardmap import' does. local function env_for(terrain) local t = TERRAIN[U.trim(tostring(terrain or "")):lower()] if not t then return nil end local rgb = PALETTE[t[2]] or PALETTE[7] pcall(setCustomEnvColor, t[1], rgb[1], rgb[2], rgb[3], 255) return t[1] end
--- -- state -- -- Declared up here on purpose. A table declared below the function that reads it -- binds a nil global instead, silently, and that has cost four separate evenings -- on this project already. ---
local current -- { id, zone, x, y, z } for the room we're standing in local lastcmd -- what was sent most recently, whatever it was local lastdir -- ...and its short direction, if it was one
local stats = { rooms = 0, exits = 0, stubs = 0, filled = 0, specials = 0, nudged = 0, stacked = 0, unexplored = 0 }
-- Room user data flag: GMCP has named this room but we've never stood in it. local UNEXPLORED = "unexplored"
M.stats = stats
-- gmcp zone key -> mudlet area. -- -- 'sure' means we read it off a room that was already in the map, which is the -- only authoritative source there is: GMCP says 'aardington' and the map says -- 'Aardington Estate', and nothing on earth connects those two strings except a -- room that is in both. -- -- Anything else is a guess, and a guess that creates an area is how you end up -- with 'aardington' sitting next to 'Aardington Estate' holding four rooms. So -- guesses stay provisional: the rooms put there are remembered, and the first -- time a known room names the real area they all move across and the guess is -- deleted. On a map with no import there is never anything to upgrade to, and -- the guess is simply the answer — which is correct for that case too. local zonearea = {}
--- -- writing ---
local function area_of(id) local ok, a = pcall(getRoomArea, id) a = ok and tonumber(a) or nil if a and a > 0 then return a end return nil end
local function resolve_zone(zone, id, info) if zone == "" then return nil end local z = zonearea[zone] if z and z.sure then return z.id end
local real = roomExists(id) and area_of(id) or nil
if real and z and real ~= z.id then for _, r in ipairs(z.mine) do pcall(setRoomArea, r, real) end pcall(deleteArea, z.id) U.note("'" .. zone .. "' is really " .. M.areaname(real) .. " - moved " .. #z.mine .. " guessed room(s) across.") zonearea[zone] = { id = real, sure = true, mine = {} } return real end if real then zonearea[zone] = { id = real, sure = true, mine = {} } return real end if z then return z.id end
local aid local ok, t = pcall(getAreaTable) if ok and type(t) == "table" then for name, a in pairs(t) do if tostring(name):lower() == zone:lower() then aid = a; break end end end if aid then zonearea[zone] = { id = aid, sure = true, mine = {} } return aid end
aid = tonumber(addAreaName(zone)) if not aid or aid < 1 then return nil end zonearea[zone] = { id = aid, sure = false, mine = {} } return aid end
local function occupied(aid, x, y, z, mine) local ok, t = pcall(getRoomsByPosition, aid, x, y, z) if not ok or type(t) ~= "table" then return false end for _, r in pairs(t) do if tonumber(r) ~= mine then return true end end return false end
local function free_spot(aid, x, y, z, id) if not aid or not occupied(aid, x, y, z, id) then return x, y, z end for mul = 1, 2 do for _, n in ipairs(NUDGE) do local nx, ny = x + n[1] * mul, y + n[2] * mul if not occupied(aid, nx, ny, z, id) then stats.nudged = stats.nudged + 1 return nx, ny, z end end end -- Sixteen tries deep and still busy. Stack it rather than wander off: an -- overlap you can see beats a room forty units away from its neighbours. stats.stacked = stats.stacked + 1 return x, y, z end
-- Hang a new room off a neighbour that's already on the map, in reverse. This is -- what saves the first room after a login, a recall, or a portal — none of which -- have a previous room to reckon from, and all of which usually drop you next to -- somewhere you've been. local function anchor(info, aid) if type(info.exits) ~= "table" or not aid then return nil end local dirs = {} for d in pairs(info.exits) do dirs[#dirs + 1] = d end table.sort(dirs) -- pairs() order is not stable; placement must be for _, d in ipairs(dirs) do local sd = M.short_dir(d) local s = sd and STEP[sd] local to = tonumber(info.exits[d]) -- An unexplored placeholder is itself sitting where we guessed it goes, -- so anchoring off one compounds a guess instead of correcting it. if s and to and roomExists(to) and area_of(to) == aid and getRoomUserData(to, UNEXPLORED) ~= "1" then local x, y, z = getRoomCoordinates(to) if x then return x - s[1], y - s[2], z - s[3] end end end return nil end
-- Best information first, guesses last. local function place(info, aid, dir) local co = info.coord if co and (tonumber(co.cont) or 0) > 0 and tonumber(co.x) and tonumber(co.y) then -- Aardwolf counts y downward, Mudlet counts it up return tonumber(co.x), -tonumber(co.y), 0 end
-- walked there in a straight line: reckon from where we were local same = current and current.zone == info.zone and current.x if same and dir and STEP[dir] then local s = STEP[dir] return current.x + s[1], current.y + s[2], current.z + s[3] end
-- Didn't walk, or didn't walk in a direction. A neighbour that's already on -- the map is a KNOWN position rather than a reckoned one, so it beats -- anything below it - and it's what saves a recall, a portal, and the first -- room after login, none of which have a direction to work from. local x, y, z = anchor(info, aid) if x then return x, y, z end
-- A special exit inside one zone with nothing known around it. It has to go -- somewhere, and a full step would claim a direction it didn't travel. if same then return current.x + 1, current.y, current.z end
return 0, 0, 0 end
-- Aardwolf paints a few room names, and a painted name stored raw is a name you -- can never search for. local function clean_name(s) return U.trim(U.strip_codes(tostring(s or ""))) end
local function detail_flags(d) if type(d) == "table" then return table.concat(d, ",") end return U.trim(tostring(d or "")) end
-- A stub is Mudlet for "there's an exit here and I don't know where it goes". -- When the room it was waiting for finally appears, fill it in — but only if -- it's still a stub. Never overwrite an exit that's already pointing somewhere. local function fill_stub(from, to, dirn) local ok, stubs = pcall(getExitStubs, from) if not ok or type(stubs) ~= "table" then return false end local short = M.short_dir(dirn) or "" for _, s in pairs(stubs) do -- older Mudlets hand back names here, newer ones numbers if tonumber(s) == dirn or tostring(s):lower() == short then pcall(setExit, from, to, dirn) stats.filled = stats.filled + 1 return true end end return false end
-- A room GMCP has named but we've never stood in. -- -- Aardwolf hands over the destination id of every exit, so an unexplored -- neighbour isn't a guess - we know its number, we just don't know anything else -- about it. Drawing it one step away with a '?' in it is what the MUSHclient map -- does, and it's the difference between "this area looks finished" and "there -- are four ways out of here I never took". -- -- It gets coordinates, an area and nothing else. Name, terrain and flags are -- filled in the moment you actually walk in, which is also when the '?' comes -- off - see the arrival path in on_move. local function sprout(from, id, sd, aid, cont) if not (CFG.unexplored and aid and id and id > 0) then return false end if roomExists(id) then return false end local s = UNIT[sd] if not s then return false end local px, py, pz = getRoomCoordinates(from) if not px then return false end
-- two apart like everything else we place, except on the continent, where -- rooms sit one apart because those coordinates come from Aardwolf local n = cont and 1 or 2 local x, y, z = px + s[1] * n, py + s[2] * n, pz + s[3]
