if not addRoom(id) then return false end x, y, z = free_spot(aid, x, y, z, id) pcall(setRoomCoordinates, id, x, y, z) pcall(setRoomArea, id, aid) pcall(setRoomUserData, id, UNEXPLORED, "1") pcall(setRoomChar, id, "?") pcall(setRoomCharColor, id, 255, 255, 255) -- the MUSHclient mapper's own dark red for a room it knows of and hasn't -- been in. style.lua owns the number; without it they just stay uncoloured. if M.UNKNOWNENV then pcall(setRoomEnv, id, M.UNKNOWNENV) end stats.unexplored = stats.unexplored + 1 return true end
local function link_exits(id, info, aid, cont) if type(info.exits) ~= "table" then return end -- pairs() order decides which unexplored neighbour claims a contested spot, -- and that shouldn't change between two identical walks local dirs = {} for d in pairs(info.exits) do dirs[#dirs + 1] = d end table.sort(dirs)
for _, d in ipairs(dirs) do local sd = M.short_dir(d) local n = sd and DIRNUM[sd] local dest = tonumber(info.exits[d]) if n then local made = false if dest and dest > 0 and not roomExists(dest) then -- draw it as a room with a '?' rather than a nub on ours made = sprout(id, dest, sd, aid, cont) if made then -- an exit back, unknown where to. A real reverse exit would -- be inventing one, and a one-way arrow into a room you've -- never seen reads as a trap that isn't there. pcall(setExitStub, dest, REVNUM[n], true) end end if dest and dest > 0 and roomExists(dest) then pcall(setExit, id, dest, n) stats.exits = stats.exits + 1 -- and the way back, if that room was still waiting on us. -- Never for one we just sprouted: that stub is the whole point, -- and filling it here would invent the exit we just refused to. if not made then fill_stub(dest, id, REVNUM[n]) end else pcall(setExitStub, id, n, true) stats.stubs = stats.stubs + 1 end end end end
--- -- the engine ---
-- Does this module write to the map? Not a preference so much as a question of -- who else is doing it: the stock module's onRoom writes on every move, and two -- writers is how rooms end up in the wrong place. With that module installed we -- only write once it has stood down; without it, nobody else is going to. function M.mapping() if not CFG.mapwrite then return false end if aard and GUIframe then return CFG.standalone and true or false end return true end
function M.why_not_mapping() if not CFG.mapwrite then return "'mapper mapping on' to switch it back on" end if aard and GUIframe and not CFG.standalone then return "the stock module is mapping - 'mapper standalone on' to take over" end return nil end
-- Every command that goes to the MUD, so dead reckoning knows which way you -- went. Ours, deliberately: the stock module keeps the same fact in aard.command -- and reading it would make this module depend on the one it replaces. function M.on_send(_, cmd) lastcmd = U.trim(tostring(cmd or "")) lastdir = M.short_dir(lastcmd) end
function M.on_move() local info = gmcp and gmcp.room and gmcp.room.info if not info then return end local id = tonumber(info.num) if not id or id < 1 then return end
local dir, cmd = lastdir, lastcmd lastdir, lastcmd = nil, nil -- consumed; the next move brings its own
local zone = tostring(info.zone or "") local prev = current
if M.mapping() and U.playing() then local aid = resolve_zone(zone, id, info) local new = not roomExists(id)
if new then addRoom(id) stats.rooms = stats.rooms + 1 local x, y, z = place(info, aid, dir) x, y, z = free_spot(aid, x, y, z, id) pcall(setRoomCoordinates, id, x, y, z) if aid then pcall(setRoomArea, id, aid) local za = zonearea[zone] if za and not za.sure then za.mine[#za.mine + 1] = id end end pcall(setRoomName, id, clean_name(info.name)) local env = env_for(info.terrain) if env then pcall(setRoomEnv, id, env) end local flags = detail_flags(info.details) if flags ~= "" then pcall(setRoomUserData, id, "info", flags) -- style.lua, if it loaded: the flags are what the symbol is -- picked from, so it has to happen after they're written if M.mark_room then M.mark_room(id) end end elseif getRoomUserData(id, UNEXPLORED) == "1" then -- A '?' we drew earlier and have now actually walked into. Its -- coordinates were reckoned from the room next door, which is the -- same arithmetic arriving would use, so they stay - everything else -- was never known and gets filled in now. pcall(clearRoomUserData, id, UNEXPLORED) pcall(setRoomChar, id, "") pcall(setRoomName, id, clean_name(info.name)) local env = env_for(info.terrain) if env then pcall(setRoomEnv, id, env) end local flags = detail_flags(info.details) if flags ~= "" then pcall(setRoomUserData, id, "info", flags) if M.mark_room then M.mark_room(id) end end stats.rooms = stats.rooms + 1 stats.unexplored = math.max(0, stats.unexplored - 1)
else -- blanks only. An imported room's name, area and coordinates are -- better than anything reckoned from here, and overwriting them is -- how a good map becomes a bad one. local okn, name = pcall(getRoomName, id) if okn and U.trim(tostring(name or "")) == "" then pcall(setRoomName, id, clean_name(info.name)) end if aid and not area_of(id) then pcall(setRoomArea, id, aid) end local oke, e = pcall(getRoomEnv, id) if not oke or (tonumber(e) or 0) < 1 then local env = env_for(info.terrain) if env then pcall(setRoomEnv, id, env) end end end
local co = info.coord link_exits(id, info, aid, co and (tonumber(co.cont) or 0) > 0)
-- the way in. GMCP already gave us this room's exits, so only the -- forward edge from where we came needs saying - the way back is either -- in that table or genuinely one-way, and guessing it is how one-way -- exits get quietly turned into two. if prev and prev.id ~= id and roomExists(prev.id) then local n = dir and DIRNUM[dir] if n then pcall(setExit, prev.id, id, n) stats.exits = stats.exits + 1 elseif CFG.autocexit and cmd and cmd ~= "" then pcall(addSpecialExit, prev.id, id, cmd) stats.specials = stats.specials + 1 end end
pcall(centerview, id) end
-- Grid mode is how the map DRAWS, not what's in it, so it happens whether or -- not this module is the one creating rooms. GMCP is the only thing that -- knows a room is on the continent, and the continent is the part that -- wants tiles rather than boxes on strings. local co = info.coord if roomExists(id) then local aid = area_of(id) if aid then -- the shops and healers in an area you've just walked into, once if M.style_area then M.style_area(aid) end -- and the room you're actually in, which every other room being a -- loud colour had made impossible to pick out if M.mark_here then M.mark_here(id) end -- keep it on top: an embedded map is drawn at absolute coordinates -- rather than inside its container, so anything can cover it if M.raise_map then M.raise_map() end if co and (tonumber(co.cont) or 0) > 0 and M.on_continent then M.on_continent(aid) end end end
local x, y, z if roomExists(id) then x, y, z = getRoomCoordinates(id) end current = { id = id, zone = zone, x = x, y = y, z = z }
-- 'mapper cexit' and 'mapper portal add' are both waiting on this same -- event, and they need the room to exist before they can link to it. One -- handler, in order, rather than two racing on pairs() order. M.on_room() end
--- -- commands ---
-- Drop everything learned about the map. The zone-to-area table holds area ids, -- and 'aardmap import' calls deleteMap() and renumbers the lot - so after an -- import every cached id points at an area that no longer exists. function M.forget() current, lastcmd, lastdir = nil, nil, nil zonearea = {} for k in pairs(stats) do stats[k] = 0 end end
function M.mapstat(rest) local v = U.trim(tostring(rest or "")):lower() if v == "forget" then M.forget() U.ok("Forgot the zone-to-area table and the room I thought you were in.") return end if v == "on" or v == "off" then CFG.mapwrite = (v == "on") M.save() local why = M.why_not_mapping() if v == "on" and why then U.warn("Switched on, but " .. why .. ".") else U.ok("Map writing " .. v .. ".") end return end
local live = M.mapping() local rows = { { "writing", live and "yes" or ("no - " .. (M.why_not_mapping() or "?")) }, { "here", current and (U.rid(current.id) .. " " .. tostring(current.zone)) or "nothing seen yet" }, { "" }, { "rooms created", tostring(stats.rooms) }, { "exits linked", tostring(stats.exits) }, { "unexplored '?'", tostring(stats.unexplored) .. (CFG.unexplored and "" or " (off)") }, { "stubs left", tostring(stats.stubs) }, { "stubs filled", tostring(stats.filled) }, } if stats.specials > 0 then rows[#rows + 1] = { "custom exits", tostring(stats.specials) } end if stats.nudged > 0 then rows[#rows + 1] = { "nudged aside", tostring(stats.nudged) } end if stats.stacked > 0 then rows[#rows + 1] = { "overlapping", tostring(stats.stacked) .. " - no free spot nearby" } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "mapper mapping on|off", "write rooms as you walk" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "mapper mapping forget", "drop the zone-to-area table (after an 'aardmap import')" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "mapper style unexplored on|off", "draw the rooms you haven't entered (" .. (CFG.unexplored and "on" or "off") .. ")" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "mapper autocexit on|off", "record non-direction moves as custom exits (" .. (CFG.autocexit and "on" or "off") .. ")" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Counts are this session only." } U.help("Mapping", rows) end
U.killhandler(aardkit_mapper_send) aardkit_mapper_send = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysDataSendRequest", "aardkit.mapper.on_send")

Script.name: mapper/style
Script.script:
--[[ Mapper — how the map draws Sean Stoves, 2026-08-02
Mudlet's default map is small rounded rooms on a grey field with exit lines strung between them. The MUSHclient Aardwolf mapper is square rooms on near-black, pale cyan exits, and a handful of loud fills for the rooms you actually go looking for. Its appearance is most of why people miss it, so this is the default rather than a command you have to find out about.
The numbers are its own, read off that plugin's settings rather than eyeballed from a screenshot - #111111 behind, #e0ffff exits, #ffad2f shops, #ffd700 banks, #9acd32 healers, #9b0000 for a room you know is there and have never stood in. None of its code is here; colours and sizes are facts about how a thing looks, and the drawing is Mudlet's own.
Four things carry the look:
* grid mode on continent areas, and only those. It fills each cell with a solid block and drops the exit lines, which is the same picture their world map is. An indoor area drawn as blocks loses the corridors, and the corridors are the shape of the place. * terrain colours, which walk.lua sets from GMCP. Their mapper tiles areas with terrain textures by default; Mudlet has no textures, and a coloured room is the nearest true thing. * fills by what a room IS - shop, healer, bank, guild - which override the terrain there and do here. In Mudlet a room's colour is its environment, so those become environments, numbered above the terrains. * a character in the same rooms, because a colour alone doesn't say which.
What this changes are Mudlet preferences, which are yours. They're written down before anything is touched and 'mapper style restore' puts them back exactly - including the terrain colour under a flag fill, which is why the old environment is parked in room user data rather than thrown away.
Room size and exit size are the two it won't touch. Their scale isn't discoverable from Mudlet's binary and guessing at somebody's map dimensions is worse than leaving them alone; 'mapper style' prints both, and 'mapper style room|exit <n>' sets them. ]]
local M = aardkit.mapper local U = aardkit.util.named("Mapper") local CFG = M.CFG
-- The preference keys, straight out of Mudlet's own getConfig list. -- -- mapRoomSize is in here now that a live 'mapper style' has said what the scale -- actually is: 0.5 by default, so it's the fraction of the cell a room fills. -- The MUSHclient mapper draws a room 12 wide with 8 between, which is 12/20 - -- 0.6, and that is the whole of the difference. -- -- mapExitSize stays out. It reads 10 against a room size of 0.5, so it is not -- the same kind of number at all - a line width in some unit of its own - and -- there is nothing in the MUSHclient settings that converts to it. local KEYS = { "mapRoundRooms", "mapShowRoomBorders", "mapShowGrid", "showRoomIdsOnMap", "show3dMapView", "showUpperLowerLevels", "mapRoomSize", }
-- Square rooms with a border, no ids painted over them, exits drawn flat. -- SHOW_ROOM_ID is off in the MUSHclient mapper's own defaults and there is no -- upper/lower-level drawing there at all, so both are off here - 'mapper style -- ids on' and setConfig put either back. local AARD = { mapRoundRooms = false, mapShowRoomBorders = true, mapShowGrid = false, showRoomIdsOnMap = false, show3dMapView = false, showUpperLowerLevels = false, mapRoomSize = 0.6, }
-- The MUSHclient mapper's own colours, read off its settings rather than -- eyeballed. Room and exit are the two Mudlet lets us set directly; the rest -- become environments below, because a room's colour in Mudlet is its -- environment and there's nowhere else to put them. local BACKGROUND = { 0x11, 0x11, 0x11 } -- #111111 local EXITS = { 0xe0, 0xff, 0xff } -- #e0ffff
-- A room's fill by what it IS, which overrides its terrain the same way it does -- there. Ids start at 200 so they can't collide with the 135 terrains. local FLAGENV = { shop = { 200, 0xff, 0xad, 0x2f }, -- #ffad2f healer = { 201, 0x9a, 0xcd, 0x32 }, -- #9acd32 trainer = { 202, 0x9a, 0xcd, 0x32 }, bank = { 203, 0xff, 0xd7, 0x00 }, -- #ffd700 guild = { 204, 0xff, 0x00, 0xff }, -- magenta quest = { 205, 0x00, 0xbf, 0xff }, -- deepskyblue safe = { 206, 0xad, 0xd8, 0xe6 }, -- lightblue }
-- Their map draws a 12-pixel room with 8 between it and the next, so one of its -- cells measures 20. Mudlet's setMapZoom is that same pixels-per-cell, which is -- why this number transfers directly - and why a saved override of 10 turned -- every room into a dot with a long line coming out of it. local ZOOM = 20
-- theirs too: a room you know is there and have never been in local UNKNOWNENV = { 207, 0x9b, 0x00, 0x00 } -- #9b0000
M.UNKNOWNENV = UNKNOWNENV[1]
-- What to stamp in a room, and which wins when a room is several things at -- once. A shop you can't find again is worse than a pk flag you forgot. -- The fill above follows the same order, so the symbol and the colour agree. local SYMORDER = { "shop", "healer", "trainer", "bank", "guild", "quest", "safe", "pk" } local SYMBOL = { shop = "$", healer = "+", trainer = "T", bank = "B", guild = "G", quest = "?", safe = "*", pk = "!", }
-- Where a room's own environment goes while a flag colour is sitting on it, so -- 'mapper style clear' can put the terrain back rather than leaving every shop -- amber for ever. A style is a preference; this one writes to the map, so it -- has to be undoable. local ENV0 = "env0"
local gridded = {} -- areas already switched to grid mode this session local stamped = {} -- ...and already marked up, so walking back in is free local lit -- the room currently wearing the you-are-here highlight
-- Their OUR_ROOM_COLOUR. Once every room is a loud flag colour, Mudlet's own -- player marker is lost in the crowd - a gold bank and a green trainer are -- exactly as bright as the room you're standing in, which makes the one thing -- you always want to find the one thing you can't. local HERE = { 0xff, 0x14, 0x93 } -- #ff1493, deeppink
--- -- symbols ---
-- the first flag this room carries, in priority order local function flag_of(id) local ok, info = pcall(getRoomUserData, id, "info") if not ok or not info or info == "" then return nil end info = "," .. info:lower() .. "," for _, flag in ipairs(SYMORDER) do if info:find("," .. flag .. ",", 1, true) then return flag end end return nil end
function M.symbol_for(id) local f = flag_of(id) return f and SYMBOL[f] or nil end
function M.mark_room(id) if not CFG.symbols then return false end local f = flag_of(id) if not f then return false end
pcall(setRoomChar, id, SYMBOL[f]) pcall(setRoomCharColor, id, 255, 255, 255)
-- and the fill, which is the half of this that reads from across the map local e = FLAGENV[f] if e then local oke, was = pcall(getRoomEnv, id) if oke and (tonumber(was) or 0) > 0 and (tonumber(was) or 0) < 200 then pcall(setRoomUserData, id, ENV0, tostring(was)) end pcall(setCustomEnvColor, e[1], e[2], e[3], e[4], 255) pcall(setRoomEnv, id, e[1]) end return true end
-- The whole map, in chunks. Declared above the function that drives it, because -- a table read from a function defined earlier binds a nil global instead. local sweep
local function sweep_step() if not sweep then return end local budget = 600 while budget > 0 do local id = sweep.rooms[sweep.i] if not id then U.ok("Marked " .. sweep.n .. " room(s) of " .. #sweep.rooms .. ".") sweep = nil return end if M.mark_room(id) then sweep.n = sweep.n + 1 end sweep.i = sweep.i + 1 budget = budget - 1 end if sweep.i - sweep.reported >= 6000 then sweep.reported = sweep.i U.note("Marking rooms... " .. sweep.i .. " of " .. #sweep.rooms) end tempTimer(0.1, sweep_step) end
-- Every room in the map, which on an imported one is 23,000 of them. Chunked -- through a timer rather than run straight: setRoomChar and setRoomEnv each -- re-render the map if the widget is open, and doing the lot in one pass is -- exactly what took the client down on the first import attempt. function M.stamp_all() if sweep then U.warn("Already marking - let it finish."); return end if not CFG.symbols then U.warn("Symbols are off. 'mapper style symbols' first."); return end local rooms = {} local ok, t = pcall(getAreaTable) if ok and type(t) == "table" then for _, aid in pairs(t) do local okr, rr = pcall(getAreaRooms, aid) if okr and type(rr) == "table" then for _, id in pairs(rr) do rooms[#rooms + 1] = id end end end end if #rooms == 0 then U.warn("No rooms in the map."); return end sweep = { rooms = rooms, i = 1, n = 0, reported = 0 } U.note("Marking " .. #rooms .. " room(s) - this runs in the background, carry on.") sweep_step() end
-- Bounded on purpose: this area, not the map. 'mapper style symbols all' does -- the lot, in chunks, because doing it in one pass is what took the client down -- on the first import attempt. local function stamp_area(aid) if not aid then return 0 end local ok, rooms = pcall(getAreaRooms, aid) if not ok or type(rooms) ~= "table" then return 0 end local n = 0 for _, id in pairs(rooms) do if M.mark_room(id) then n = n + 1 end end return n end
-- Highlight the room you're in and let go of the last one. -- -- A highlight is stored in the map, so the previous one has to be released or -- they accumulate and every room you have ever entered stays pink. function M.mark_here(id) id = tonumber(id) if lit and lit ~= id then pcall(unHighlightRoom, lit) -- it was wearing a flag symbol before we lit it; put that back if CFG.symbols then M.mark_room(lit) end lit = nil end if not id or CFG.style ~= "aard" then return false end if not U.has("highlightRoom") then return false end if lit == id then return true end -- A RING, not a fill. Their map keeps the room's own colour and draws the -- pink around it, so you can still see you're standing in a shop - filling -- it solid throws away the one fact the colour was carrying. -- -- highlightRoom(id, outer rgb, inner rgb, radius, outer alpha, inner alpha). -- Radius is a multiple of the room, so 1.5 spills just past its edge, and an -- inner alpha of 0 leaves the middle clear for the room to show through. local ok = pcall(highlightRoom, id, HERE[1], HERE[2], HERE[3], HERE[1], HERE[2], HERE[3], 1.5, 255, 0) if ok then lit = id end return ok end
-- Every area you walk into, once. -- -- style_apply on load can only do the settings - there's no room to stand in -- yet, so no area to mark. That left the map drawn right but unmarked until -- 'mapper style aard' was typed, which is a default that isn't one. function M.style_area(aid) if CFG.style ~= "aard" then return 0 end aid = tonumber(aid) if not aid or stamped[aid] then return 0 end stamped[aid] = true
-- Zoom, on entering the area rather than once at load. Mudlet keeps it per -- area, so setting it in Aylor left every other area on whatever it had - -- which is why one area drew proper rooms and the next drew dots joined by -- lines. Same number everywhere: 20 is one MUSHclient cell in pixels. if U.has("setMapZoom") then pcall(setMapZoom, ZOOM) end
-- An area we gridded earlier stays gridded - setGridMode writes to the map -- and outlives the session. Grid is the continent's now, so an ordinary area -- that still has it gets it taken off, or it keeps the solid-block drawing -- from a version of this that gridded wherever you happened to stand. if not gridded[aid] and U.has("setGridMode") and U.has("getGridMode") then local okg, on = pcall(getGridMode, aid) if okg and on then pcall(setGridMode, aid, false) end end
if not CFG.symbols then return 0 end return stamp_area(aid) end
--- -- grid mode ---
local function area_here() local id = getPlayerRoom and getPlayerRoom() if not id or id == -1 then id = U.room() end if not id then return nil end local ok, a = pcall(getRoomArea, id) a = ok and tonumber(a) or nil if a and a > 0 then return a end return nil end
function M.grid(aid, on) if not U.has("setGridMode") then return false end aid = tonumber(aid) if not aid then return false end local ok = pcall(setGridMode, aid, on and true or false) if ok then gridded[aid] = on and true or nil end return ok end
-- walk.lua calls this the first time it sees a continent room in an area. The -- continent is the bit that looks wrong drawn as boxes-and-strings, and it's -- also the only bit we can identify without asking - GMCP flags it. function M.on_continent(aid) if not CFG.autogrid or not aid or gridded[aid] then return end if M.grid(aid, true) then U.note("Continent area drawn as tiles - 'mapper style grid off' if you'd rather not.") end end
--- -- applying ---
-- Records anything not recorded yet, rather than all-or-nothing. A key added to -- KEYS after somebody already had a snapshot would never be captured otherwise, -- and 'mapper style restore' would quietly not restore it. local function snapshot() if not U.has("getConfig") then return end local was = CFG.stylewas or {} local added = false -- zoom isn't a getConfig key, it has its own pair of functions if was.zoom == nil and U.has("getMapZoom") then local okz, z = pcall(getMapZoom) if okz and tonumber(z) then was.zoom = tonumber(z); added = true end end for _, k in ipairs(KEYS) do if was[k] == nil then local ok, v = pcall(getConfig, k) if ok and v ~= nil then was[k] = v; added = true end end end if added then CFG.stylewas = was; M.save() end end
local function apply(tbl) if not U.has("setConfig") then U.warn("This Mudlet has no setConfig, so the map settings can't be changed from here.") return false end for k, v in pairs(tbl) do if k == "zoom" then if U.has("setMapZoom") then pcall(setMapZoom, v) end else pcall(setConfig, k, v) end end return true end
-- The settings half, with nothing that needs a room to stand in. Called on load, -- because 'aard' is the default style now and a default you have to type isn't -- one. Room size and exit size are deliberately absent - they're the two values -- whose scale I couldn't establish from the binary, and guessing at somebody's -- map dimensions is worse than leaving them where they are. 'mapper style' -- prints both, 'mapper style room|exit <n>' sets them. function M.style_apply() snapshot() if not apply(AARD) then return false end pcall(setMapBackgroundColor, BACKGROUND[1], BACKGROUND[2], BACKGROUND[3]) pcall(setMapRoomExitsColor, EXITS[1], EXITS[2], EXITS[3]) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, UNKNOWNENV[1], UNKNOWNENV[2], UNKNOWNENV[3], UNKNOWNENV[4], 255) if U.has("setMapZoom") then pcall(setMapZoom, ZOOM) end return true end
function M.style_aard(quiet) if not M.style_apply() then return end CFG.style = "aard" CFG.symbols = true CFG.autogrid = true M.save()
local aid = area_here() if aid then stamped[aid] = nil -- re-do this area, whatever it had before M.style_area(aid) end local n = stamp_area(aid) -- deliberately NOT gridding this area. Grid mode is for the continent and -- nothing else: an indoor area drawn as solid blocks loses its exit lines, -- and with them every door, every one-way, and the difference between two -- rooms that connect and two that merely sit next to each other. -- M.on_continent handles the continent, off GMCP, per area.
if quiet then return end M.mark_here(select(1, U.room())) U.ok("Map drawn the MUSHclient way - its background, its exit colour, square rooms, " .. "and shops, healers and banks in its colours.") U.note("Marked " .. n .. " room(s) in this area. 'mapper style symbols' does the next one.") U.note("'mapper style restore' puts your own settings back.") end
function M.style_restore() local was = CFG.stylewas or {} if not next(was) then U.note("Nothing saved to go back to - the style was never applied."); return end apply(was) for aid in pairs(gridded) do pcall(setGridMode, aid, false) end gridded = {} CFG.style, CFG.symbols, CFG.autogrid = "", false, false CFG.stylewas = {} M.save() U.ok("Map settings put back the way they were.") end
--- -- the command ---
function M.style(rest) local verb, more = U.split_verb(rest) more = U.trim(more)
if verb == "aard" or verb == "world" or verb == "mushclient" then M.style_aard()
elseif verb == "restore" or verb == "default" or verb == "mudlet" then M.style_restore()
elseif verb == "grid" then local on = more:lower() ~= "off" local aid = area_here() if not aid then U.warn("Mudlet doesn't know which area you're in."); return end if M.grid(aid, on) then U.ok(M.areaname(aid) .. " drawn as " .. (on and "solid tiles." or "rooms and exit lines.")) else U.warn("This Mudlet has no setGridMode.") end
elseif verb == "symbols" then if more:lower() == "all" then CFG.symbols = true; M.save() M.stamp_all() return end if more == "off" then CFG.symbols = false; M.save() U.ok("Room symbols off. They stay on rooms already marked - 'mapper style clear' removes them.") return end CFG.symbols = true; M.save() local n = stamp_area(area_here()) U.ok("Marked " .. n .. " room(s) in this area.")
elseif verb == "clear" then local ok, rooms = pcall(getAreaRooms, area_here()) local n = 0 if ok and type(rooms) == "table" then for _, id in pairs(rooms) do -- the '?' on an unexplored room isn't a symbol, it's the room local oku, u = pcall(getRoomUserData, id, "unexplored") if not (oku and u == "1") then pcall(setRoomChar, id, "") -- and the terrain colour back from under the flag colour local okz, was = pcall(getRoomUserData, id, ENV0) if okz and tonumber(was) then pcall(setRoomEnv, id, tonumber(was)) pcall(clearRoomUserData, id, ENV0) end n = n + 1 end end end U.ok("Cleared symbols and flag colours from " .. n .. " room(s) in this area.")
elseif verb == "autogrid" then CFG.autogrid = more:lower() ~= "off"; M.save() U.ok("Continent areas drawn as tiles when first seen: " .. (CFG.autogrid and "on" or "off")) if not CFG.autogrid then U.note("Areas already switched stay that way - 'mapper style grid off' per area.") end
elseif verb == "unexplored" then CFG.unexplored = more:lower() ~= "off"; M.save() U.ok("Rooms GMCP knows about but you haven't entered: " .. (CFG.unexplored and "drawn with a '?'" or "not drawn")) if not CFG.unexplored then U.note("The ones already on the map stay - they fill in when you walk into them.") end
elseif verb == "ids" then pcall(setConfig, "showRoomIdsOnMap", more:lower() ~= "off") U.ok("Room ids on the map: " .. (more:lower() ~= "off" and "on" or "off"))
elseif verb == "room" or verb == "exit" then local n = tonumber(more) local key = verb == "room" and "mapRoomSize" or "mapExitSize" if not n then local okc, cur = pcall(getConfig, key) U.warn("Usage: mapper style " .. verb .. " <number> (currently " .. (okc and tostring(cur) or "?") .. ")") return end pcall(setConfig, key, n) U.ok(key .. " = " .. n)
else local cur = {} if U.has("getConfig") then for _, k in ipairs(KEYS) do local ok, v = pcall(getConfig, k) cur[k] = ok and tostring(v) or "?" end local okr, rs = pcall(getConfig, "mapRoomSize") local oke, es = pcall(getConfig, "mapExitSize") cur.mapRoomSize = okr and tostring(rs) or "?" cur.mapExitSize = oke and tostring(es) or "?" end U.help("mapper style", { { "style", CFG.style ~= "" and CFG.style or "yours, untouched" }, { "symbols", CFG.symbols and "on" or "off" }, { "auto grid", CFG.autogrid and "continent areas become tiles" or "off" }, { "unexplored", CFG.unexplored and "drawn with a '?'" or "off" }, { "" }, { "round rooms", cur.mapRoundRooms or "?" }, { "room borders", cur.mapShowRoomBorders or "?" }, { "room ids", cur.showRoomIdsOnMap or "?" }, { "room size", cur.mapRoomSize or "?" }, { "zoom", (U.has("getMapZoom") and tostring(select(2, pcall(getMapZoom)))) or "?" .. "" }, { "exit size", cur.mapExitSize or "?" }, { "" }, { "mapper style aard", "the MUSHclient look - on by default, this re-applies it" }, { "mapper style restore", "put your own settings back" }, { "mapper style grid on|off", "this area as solid tiles, or not" }, { "mapper style autogrid on|off", "do that automatically on the continent" }, { "mapper style unexplored on|off", "draw rooms GMCP knows and you haven't entered" }, { "mapper style symbols [off]", "mark shops, healers and the rest in this area" }, { "mapper style symbols all", "every room in the map, in chunks - do this once" }, { "mapper style clear", "take the symbols off this area" }, { "mapper style ids on|off", "room numbers painted on the map" }, { "mapper style room|exit <n>", "the two sizes, left alone by the presets" }, { "" }, { "Grid mode is per area, which is the point: the continent wants tiles" }, { "and an inn does not." }, }) end end
-- The style is on by default, so it applies itself. Only the settings half: -- marking rooms needs a room to be standing in and there isn't one yet. -- -- Behind a timer for the same reason the map claim is - the stock module builds -- its frame on a 0.1s delay, and anything touching map settings before that is -- racing it. Once, not on every reload of this script. -- The unknown-room colour is registered straight away rather than inside the -- timer below: walk.lua can sprout a '?' room on the first GMCP packet, and an -- environment with no colour registered draws as nothing in particular. pcall(setCustomEnvColor, UNKNOWNENV[1], UNKNOWNENV[2], UNKNOWNENV[3], UNKNOWNENV[4], 255)
if CFG.style == "aard" and not aardkit_mapper_styled then aardkit_mapper_styled = true tempTimer(2, function() M.style_apply() end) end
